title: Corpus never reached curation closure
evidence_summary: paper.eligibility_status = pending 447, duplicate 6; paper.inclusion_decision = pending 447, exclude 6; paper.annotation_status = not_started 453; paper.reviewer unpopulated; human_review table has 0 rows.
affected_proportion: 447/453 papers (98.7%) carry no inclusion decision; 453/453 carry no annotation status.
scientific_impact: The corpus is presented as 453 human-microbiome papers, but the recorded state is "gathered", not "screened". Readiness claims that depend on a screened corpus are unsupported by the record.
publication_impact: A reviewer who opens paper and sees pending × 447 will ask how inclusion was decided. The answer must be documentary, not narrative.
recommended_action: Do not backfill retroactively with new judgments (that would be new annotation). Either (a) state explicitly in the manuscript that inclusion was a retrieval criterion, not a screening decision, and describe the criterion; or (b) record the historical criterion as inclusion_decision with its evidence, clearly labelled as reconstructed. Option (a) is honest and requires no new science.
blocking_status: blocks submission (as an unstated claim), not public release.

title: Six duplicate paper rows remain in the CDM
evidence_summary: 441 distinct DOIs across 447 DOI-bearing papers; 5 duplicate groups / 6 extra rows (10.1038/sdata.2018.68 ×3; four groups of ×2). All six carry is_canonical=false and eligibility_status=duplicate.
scientific_impact: Low for aggregates already filtered to is_canonical, but any query that joins paper without a canonical filter double-counts those papers' entities, sections and claims.
publication_impact: Paper-level counts quoted from unfiltered joins will be slightly wrong.
recommended_action: Document the canonical filter requirement prominently; do not delete (retaining duplicates with a flag is the correct design). Verify every headline count was taken over is_canonical=1 or is deliberately over 453.
blocking_status: neither, provided the filter is documented.

title: Eight-six percent of papers self-declare REVIEW_REQUIRED
evidence_summary: validation_status REVIEW_REQUIRED 392 / COMPLETE 46 / PARTIAL 15; full_text_completeness partial 407 / complete 46; sections_needing_review 1,242 of 4,006.
scientific_impact: The corpus layer's own validator did not reach a clean state for most papers. Downstream components inherit this without a compensating control.
publication_impact: Reporting "453 papers" without this flag overstates corpus cleanliness.
recommended_action: Report the validation distribution in the manuscript's data-availability section rather than a bare count. Do not attempt to close these flags in this audit cycle.
blocking_status: neither; it is a reporting requirement.

title: Licence absent from the corpus record itself
evidence_summary: paper.license_name NULL for 453/453; reuse_permission_checked = unclear for 453/453. Licence data exists only in paper/publication/rights/PAPER_RIGHTS_MATRIX.csv (Component N).
scientific_impact: None directly.
publication_impact: Two records now disagree in spirit — the CDM says "unclear" while the rights matrix asserts a specific licence for 318 papers. Anyone using the CDM alone will conclude reuse permission was never assessed.
recommended_action: Note in the data dictionary that rights are held externally and that reuse_permission_checked=unclear is a not-assessed sentinel, not a finding of no permission.

title: Encoding defects and metadata conflicts
evidence_summary: source_integrity: 4 papers contain U+0000 bytes (HMPAPER_000446 from the PRJNA750230/413199/307231/486009 family); papers_with_metadata_conflicts = 52.
scientific_impact: NUL bytes are documented ligature artefacts and are slice-exact, so offsets remain valid; they are a display/parse hazard, not a corruption.
publication_impact: Any consumer reading these four files as UTF-8 text without NUL handling will see truncated strings.
recommended_action: Document the four paper IDs and the NUL handling rule; do not rewrite the markdown (hash-pinned by 2.2.0).

title: Identifier gaps
evidence_summary: 6 papers without DOI, 13 without PMID, 100 without PMCID, 40 without abstract, 6 without title.
scientific_impact: PMC-only retrieval and any DOI-keyed join will drop those papers.
publication_impact: Minor; should be stated if identifier-based linkage is quoted.
recommended_action: Report identifier coverage alongside paper count.

title: Dated amendment disclosing that SQLite LENGTH() and Python len() give two different corpus character totals and two different zero-section counts (26,874,831 / 453 vs 26,781,631 / 454)
evidence_summary: 01_CORPUS_QUALITY.md header stated 26,874,831 section characters and the section 1 'Semantic quality' row stated 'exactly 453 zero-char front/(preamble) placeholders'. Both reproduce under a Python read (con.text_factory = bytes, then .decode('utf-8','replace')). SQLite SUM(LENGTH(section_text_original)) on the same frozen DB gives 26,781,631 characters and 454 zero-length rows. Delta 93,200 chars / 1 row, caused by 14 sections in 4 papers carrying U+0000 (the documented upstream PDF ligature artifact). The extra SQL-zero row is HMPAPER_000120/sec_gap_000, which is 4,310 chars long and begins with U+0000 so LENGTH() returns 0; the other 13 are truncated by LENGTH(), not zeroed. Per-row table is in the amendment record.
affected_proportion: 1 clause in the section 1 dimension table plus a section 5 amendment record in 01_CORPUS_QUALITY.md; no count in any other report is superseded and no artefact modified
scientific_impact: None. The audit's own 453 is the semantically correct figure (453 structurally-expected front/(preamble) placeholders). The exposure is that a SQL consumer sees 454 empty sections and cannot reproduce term_mention offsets with a naive SQL substr() into the 14 affected sections.
publication_impact: Prevents a reviewer or reuser from 'discovering' an apparent discrepancy between the manuscript's corpus size and a SQL query, and records which denominator underlies the withheld-share percentages (37.24% on the SQL total, 37.11% on the Python total).
recommended_action: Applied 2026-11-05: parenthetical marker added in place, superseded wording retained, section 5 amendment record added to report 01 with the full 14-row table and both reproducing commands. Report 01's ratings are unchanged.
blocking_status: neither; caveat disclosed. No register row value moved.

title: en_core_sci_lg emits a single generic label for 38% of all mentions
evidence_summary: error_signature for en_core_sci_lg: 960,674 rows, 151,186 distinct surfaces, 1 distinct type. Every mention is labelled ENTITY.
scientific_impact: Because it is the largest single source, the terminology layer's type distribution is dominated by an untyped contributor. This is the mechanical origin of the 55.29% ENTITY share in Component C. Any per-type analysis inherits it.
publication_impact: Type-coverage figures that include this source are inflated toward ENTITY by construction, not by biology.
recommended_action: Either exclude en_core_sci_lg from typed analyses and say so, or report type distributions both with and without it. Do not present a single blended type mix as if all sources were typed.
blocking_status: blocks submission of any per-type claim presented without this caveat.

title: 156,870 mentions required offset re-derivation
evidence_summary: offset_status = CORRECTED 156,870 (6.26%). The stored start_offset/end_offset did not index the recorded term in the recorded section.
scientific_impact: Anyone who used the stored offsets without re-checking would have been wrong about 1 mention in 16. The audit's re-anchoring recovered them, but the frozen artefact still holds the original values.
publication_impact: Any published claim of "offsets are exact" must be corrected to "93.74% exact, 6.26% re-derived, 0.002% unanchored".
recommended_action: Report the three-way offset status. Do not silently overwrite.
blocking_status: neither; it is a reporting correction.

title: Qwen rows are not bit-reproducible
evidence_summary: vLLM at temperature=0 is not deterministic on this hardware; documented during the section-cache repair (retries failed at identical character offsets and recovered different rows). 552,147 rows (22.03%) originate from the two Qwen runs.
scientific_impact: The artefact is fixed and internally consistent; a future re-run will differ in tail cases.
publication_impact: "Fully reproducible" would be false for this 22%.
recommended_action: Describe Qwen output as a frozen checkpointed artefact with recorded cache, not as a reproducible computation.

title: Surface-form noise concentrated in specific classes
evidence_summary: generic_surface 150,869; numeric_only 16,315; single_char 9,239; punctuation-adjacent 5,498; over_200_chars 89.
affected_proportion: up to 150,869+ (6.0%) for the generic class alone.
scientific_impact: Generic surfaces ("group", "samples", "data") are mention-level noise that inflates totals and pollutes term groups.
publication_impact: Mention totals carry a noise floor of roughly 6%.
recommended_action: Report the generic-surface count; provide a documented filter expression rather than a silently filtered number.

title: 11.97% of mentions resolve to no canonical term [corrected 2026-11-05 — the remainder was mislabelled by including AMBIGUOUS in neither complement; see §6, CQA-B-AMEND-2026-11-05-1]
evidence_summary: term_link_status NO_CANONICAL_TERM 299,846; AMBIGUOUS 7,072; LINKED_BY_TYPE 30,049; LINKED 2,168,717. canonical_term_id IS NOT NULL = 2,198,766 (LINKED + LINKED_BY_TYPE).
affected_proportion: 299,846/2,505,684 = 11.97% carry no canonical term and are not ambiguous; 7,072 (0.28%) are ambiguous. Together 306,918 = 12.25% do not resolve to a unique term; 87.75% do.
scientific_impact: Term-level statistics silently exclude 12.25% of extracted mentions. If the unlinked 12% is non-random (likely — rare or malformed surfaces fail to link), term counts are biased toward well-formed common terms.
publication_impact: Terminology coverage claims must state the 12.25% remainder. The register's M13 87.8% is the correct linked figure and agrees with this one (87.75%); the 11.97% must not be presented as the whole remainder.
recommended_action: Quantify the unlinked remainder's surface distribution; report it as a named residual rather than assuming it is negligible.

title: 56 permanently unanchored mentions
evidence_summary: offset_status = UNANCHORED for 56 rows; they carry no usable start/end or fall outside the section text.
scientific_impact: Negligible.
publication_impact: None, if disclosed.
recommended_action: Report as a residual; exclude from span-based work by filtering offset_status != 'UNANCHORED'.

title: Sources are partially redundant, not fully complementary
evidence_summary: Within-model duplicate span rate ≈0, but cross-model overlap is unquantified in this audit; the frozen comparison reports global inter-model agreement 0.223 (full-body) and 0.156 (historical Ollama) at shared-unit level.
scientific_impact: "Multi-NER ensemble" implies complementarity. Measured agreement of 0.22 suggests substantial divergence — which is either complementarity or mutual error; this audit cannot distinguish them.
publication_impact: The ensemble framing needs the agreement figure attached.
recommended_action: Report inter-model agreement as measured (0.223 full-body / 0.156 historical), explicitly noted as agreement and not accuracy.

title: Dated amendment correcting report 02's linkage percentage, which counted only the LINKED status token and omitted LINKED_BY_TYPE (86.55% -> 87.75%)
evidence_summary: 02_ENTITY_EXTRACTION_QUALITY.md section 1 'Reusability' row and CQA-B-06 reported 'term_link_status resolves 2,168,717 (86.55%) to a canonical term' and '299,846/2,505,684 = 11.97% unlinked'. Verified read-only in releases/cdm_v3/3.0.3/microbiome_cdm_v3.db: canonical_term_id IS NOT NULL on 2,198,766 rows = LINKED 2,168,717 + LINKED_BY_TYPE 30,049 = 87.75%; NO_CANONICAL_TERM 299,846 (11.97%) + AMBIGUOUS 7,072 (0.28%). The four classes sum to 2,505,684 exactly. LINKED_BY_TYPE is a real resolution (fix_terminology_offsets.py:13,83; cdm_remediation/build_dictionary.py:57) that also carries a canonical_term_id, so the original figure understated linkage by 1.20 points.
affected_proportion: 2 figure sentences plus the remainder label in 02_ENTITY_EXTRACTION_QUALITY.md; no rating changed and no count in any other report is superseded
scientific_impact: None to any underlying value; all four status counts were and remain correct. The correction aligns report 02 with the manuscript's own M13/M10 87.8% claim, which was correct all along.
publication_impact: Prevents a reviewer comparing report 02's 86.55% against the manuscript's 87.8% from concluding either that the manuscript overstates linkage or that the audit disagrees with it.
recommended_action: Applied 2026-11-05: superseded wording retained with an inline marker, section 6 amendment record added to report 02 with the four-class count table and both reproducer queries. Reusability stays ADEQUATE and CQA-B-06 stays MODERATE.
blocking_status: neither; correction applied. No register row value moved.

title: Type vocabulary diverges from the declared CDM vocabulary
evidence_summary: cdm_type_not_in_declared_vocabulary = ["CELL_TYPE","DATA_ANALYSIS","DNA_RNA","GENOMICS","LAB_METHOD","PATHWAY","SAMPLE_METHOD","STUDY_DESIGN"]; these carry 31,864 terms / 181,392 mentions.
scientific_impact: Every per-type analysis in the project (catalogue type distributions, triple entity types, KG edge typing) is computed over an undocumented 15-value vocabulary while the code and the data dictionary advertise 14. Any claim of the form "X% of terms are type Y" is only valid relative to the observed vocabulary.
publication_impact: A reviewer cross-checking CDM_TYPES against the released data finds an inconsistency immediately. It reads as a schema violation.
recommended_action: Do not remap now (that would change frozen records). In the released documentation, publish the observed 15-value typology with the 8 extensions explicitly declared as extensions, and state that config.py:CDM_TYPES reflects the original 14 and needs alignment in a future version. Add a validation rule for version 4.
blocking_status: blocks submission until disclosed; blocks public release until documented.

title: ENTITY holds 55.29% of terms
evidence_summary: 89,799 terms / 285,399 mentions typed ENTITY; 960,674 mentions (38.3% of all) come from the single-labelled en_core_sci_lg source.
scientific_impact: Slightly more than half the terminology layer is untyped. Entity-type-based reasoning — a headline capability of a CDM — is available for the other 44.7%.
publication_impact: Type-coverage tables must be read as "typed subset" tables.
recommended_action: Report typed coverage as 72,610/162,409 = 44.71%, and state the ENTITY mass's origin. Do not present the blended mix.
blocking_status: blocks any per-type claim stated over all 162,409 terms.

title: Type provenance recorded for 3.06% of terms
evidence_summary: type_source NULL 157,446; deepseek+alternative_seen 3,676; deepseek+gemma 1,287.
scientific_impact: For 96.94% of terms there is no record of whether the type came from a model, a gazetteer, a rule, or a default. The type field is therefore not auditable at row level.
publication_impact: Methods text cannot truthfully describe the typing procedure for the bulk of the vocabulary.
recommended_action: Describe typing as "assigned during canonicalisation; per-term provenance not retained" — an honest limitation. Do not reconstruct provenance.
blocking_status: blocks a methods claim of per-term type provenance.

title: The generic-type flag contradicts the type on 57.6% of rows
evidence_summary: is_generic_type_flag = 93,580 rows; flag_vs_type_disagreement = 93,580 (identical count — the flag disagrees in exactly the rows where it is set).
scientific_impact: Two fields purport to describe the same property and disagree in the majority of flagged rows. A consumer cannot tell which is authoritative.
publication_impact: Any "generic term" statistic is ambiguous.
recommended_action: Document the flag's semantics precisely (it appears to mean "type is not specific enough to be useful", not "type is ENTITY"). Provide the exact filter expression for each intended use.

title: 9,940 live terms have no mention and 3,184 removed terms still carry live mentions
evidence_summary: term_mention join: 152,469 of 162,409 live terms carry ≥1 mention (D02 orphan count 9,940). removed_terms_with_live_mentions = 3,184 of 3,582 (88.9%).
affected_proportion: 6.12% of live terms unsupported; 88.9% of removed terms still referenced.
scientific_impact: A live term with no mention has no corpus evidence at all — it exists only in the vocabulary. A removed term with live mentions means 13,927 mentions (per D02) point at a tombstone.
publication_impact: "Every term is grounded in the corpus" is false for 9,940 terms.
recommended_action: Report both residuals. The tombstone design is defensible (removal is recorded, not deleted); what must not be claimed is that the live set is fully grounded.

title: 9,647 ORGANISM terms lack taxonomic shape; no TAXON type exists
evidence_summary: binomial_like 18,138 vs type_ORGANISM_rows 12,026; organism_rows_without_binomial_shape 9,647; type_TAXON_rows = 0; strain_designation_rows 801.
scientific_impact: ORGANISM appears to hold everything from species binomials to study cohorts ("patients", "mice"), with no separate taxon rank and no strain type. Taxonomic specificity — a core microbiome requirement — is not represented in the type system.
publication_impact: Any claim about taxonomic resolution at term level is unsupported.
recommended_action: State that taxonomic rank is not modelled in 1.0.1/3.0.3; defer to a future version.

title: Removal rationale absent for 93.4% of removed terms
evidence_summary: non_concept_reason NULL 3,344 / 3,582; populated for URL_OR_LICENSE 156, CONTROL_CHAR 59, FIGURE_TABLE_REF 14, SIGNIFICANCE_MARKER 9.
scientific_impact: The removal step is largely unexplained, so a reader cannot tell whether removed entries were non-concepts or merely unlucky.
publication_impact: Cannot defend the word "non-term" for 3,344 entries.
recommended_action: Describe removed entries as "removed during canonicalisation; reason not retained for 93.4%". Do not call them all non-terms.

title: Under-merging of plural forms not detected
evidence_summary: undermerge_plural_count_at_least = 0; undermerge_plural_examples empty.
scientific_impact: None found. Recorded here because the audit tested for it and the result is a genuine negative.
publication_impact: none.
recommended_action: none.

title: 68 term_norm groups hold multiple surfaces, including control characters
evidence_summary: term_norm_groups_with_multiple_surfaces = 68; examples include -diversity, 80oc/80°c freezer, NUL/control-character artefacts; removed_reason_non_concept_reason includes CONTROL_CHAR 59.
scientific_impact: Negligible volume; the NUL cases trace to the four papers in Component A.
publication_impact: none.
recommended_action: document the control-character normalisation rule.

title: The mapping was never re-queried and cannot be regenerated
evidence_summary: mapping_provenance literal value "projected from an existing linking run; not re-queried" on 331,394/331,394 rows (100%); mapping_evidence_status = RESTORED on 100%; no per-row service version; matched_via NULL on 93.63%.
scientific_impact: Every ontology link in the release is a restored copy whose originating query is not recorded. If the originating run was wrong, the release is wrong in a way no stored field can reveal.
publication_impact: "Mappings validated against UMLS/OLS/BioPortal" cannot be claimed. What can be claimed is "mappings reused from an earlier linking run; not re-queried for this release".
recommended_action: State the reuse-first design plainly in the methods and in the mapping table's own documentation. Do not describe these as fresh lookups. A future version should re-query a stratified sample and report the agreement rate.
blocking_status: blocks any methods statement implying fresh validation. Does not block public release if disclosed.

title: 87.52% of mapping rows are REVIEW_REQUIRED
evidence_summary: mapping_disposition REVIEW_REQUIRED 290,021 / REJECTED 30,693 / UNRESOLVED 10,680. human_review table: 0 rows.
scientific_impact: The mapping table is a candidate set, not an adjudicated mapping. Treating it as a mapping overstates what exists.
publication_impact: Any "X% of terms mapped to ontology concepts" must specify the disposition filter.
recommended_action: Publish the table as candidates with disposition labels intact; never strip the disposition column in an export.
blocking_status: blocks claims of an adjudicated mapping.

title: 5,431 EXACT_MATCH rows have a non-identical label
evidence_summary: relation_vs_label_identity: EXACT_MATCH|label_differs = 5,431; EXACT_MATCH|label_identical = 26,356. Also AMBIGUOUS|label_identical = 32,078.
affected_proportion: 5,431 rows (1.64% of all rows; 17.09% of EXACT_MATCH rows).
scientific_impact: An "exact match" between different strings is only defensible as synonymy, and the table records no synonym evidence per row (matched_via is populated for 6.37%). Conversely, 32,078 rows are called AMBIGUOUS while the labels are identical — the reverse contradiction.
publication_impact: The mapping_relation field cannot be presented as a validated equivalence relation.
recommended_action: Describe mapping_relation as a model-assigned label, not a lexical verdict. Provide the label-identity cross-tab so users can filter.
blocking_status: blocks presenting mapping_relation as validated equivalence.

title: Model-verdict labels are corrupted by mid-token truncation
evidence_summary: relation_deepseek contains WRS, RELADED, WORNG, REATED, WORM, WRIGHT, WRONG — all mid-token truncations of WRONG/RELATED/WORD; the identical defect appears in relation.verdict_deepseek (224 off-vocabulary of 25,788, 0.87%) and term_definition.verdict_deepseek (107 off-vocabulary of 6,773, 1.58%, including MENTIO from MENTIONED and DEFIN from DEFINITION).
affected_proportion: all three verdict columns, at 0.87%–1.58% of their rows.
scientific_impact: A consumer filtering verdict_deepseek='WRONG' misses WORNG, WRS, WORM, WRIGHT. Filtering ='SUPPORTED' is safe; filtering any negative class is not. The corruption is silent.
publication_impact: Any count of model-negative verdicts is understated by the truncated remainder.
recommended_action: Ship a documented verdict vocabulary per column and a list of off-vocabulary observed values, so consumers can coalesce them. Do not silently rewrite the frozen values.
blocking_status: blocks any negative-verdict count quoted as exact.

title: More than half the vocabulary was never mapped
evidence_summary: 85,663/162,409 live terms (52.74%) have no term_concept_map row of any kind.
scientific_impact: Ontology-based reasoning applies to at most 47.26% of the vocabulary. Because unmapped terms are likely also the rare/malformed ones, the mapped subset is biased toward well-formed common concepts.
publication_impact: "Terms are linked to standard ontologies" must be qualified with the 47.26% figure.
recommended_action: Report term-level mapping coverage, not row-level. Distinguish "no candidate found" (11,477) from "never queried" (85,663) — these are different claims and the release currently conflates them.

title: Concept namespace is unattributable for 90.7% of concepts
evidence_summary: concept.ontology_name NULL for 185,822/204,817 (90.72%); term_concept_map has no ontology_source column. concept does carry source_service (ols 62,383 / bioportal 61,280 / umls 54,381 / omop 18,995 / mesh 6,613 / ncbi_taxon 1,165).
scientific_impact: A concept can be traced to a service but not to an ontology for 9 in 10 rows. "SNOMED", "MESH", "MONDO" appear for only 9.3% of concepts.
publication_impact: Ontology-level statistics are not obtainable from the release.
recommended_action: State that source_service is the attributable field and ontology_name is sparse. Do not aggregate by ontology_name without stating the 90.7% NULL.

title: 49,044 terms hold multiple accepted candidates
evidence_summary: terms_with_multi_accepted = 49,044 of 76,746 mapped terms (63.9%); candidate_rank distributes up to 11+; is_canonical_candidate = 1 on 60,352 rows across those terms.
scientific_impact: Candidate proliferation without adjudication means "the" mapping of a term does not exist for most mapped terms.
publication_impact: A one-term-one-concept claim is unsupported.
recommended_action: Document that the table is ranked candidates; provide the candidate_rank=1 AND is_canonical_candidate=1 filter as the documented single-link view, with its caveats.

title: 5,237 rows point at terms that are not in the terminology release
evidence_summary: term_status = NOT_IN_TERMINOLOGY on 5,237 rows; this is an explicit self-label, so it is honest.
scientific_impact: These rows resolve to no term. They are not anonymous — the status names the condition.
publication_impact: none, if disclosed.
recommended_action: Report the population as "links resolving to no term" alongside the 11,473 REMOVED rows.

title: Guard rejections are recorded but unexplained per row
evidence_summary: guard_status kept 314,772 / rejected_guard 16,622; guard_rejection_reason column exists.
scientific_impact: Low; the guard did fire and did record.
publication_impact: none.
recommended_action: document the guard rule set.

title: Definitions cover 2.09% of the vocabulary
evidence_summary: 3,397 distinct term_id with ≥1 definition vs 162,409 live terms.
scientific_impact: The CDM cannot serve as a defined vocabulary. Any downstream use that assumes a definition exists — glossary generation, concept disambiguation, human-readable entity explanation — fails for 97.9% of terms.
publication_impact: "The CDM provides definitions for its terms" must be rewritten as "provides definitions for 2.09% of its terms". This is a material claim change.
recommended_action: State coverage as a headline limitation. Do not present the 6,773 figure without its denominator in the same sentence. Defer expansion to a future version.
blocking_status: blocks any definitional-completeness claim; does not block release if disclosed.

title: 551 definitions do not contain the term they define
evidence_summary: definition_content_checks.term_absent_from_definition = 551 (8.14%); concentrated in CONTEXTUAL_DESCRIPTION at 447/473 (94.5%); the same class also supplies the term-in-definition rate of 26/473 (5.5%).
scientific_impact: These rows mislabel a passage as a definition of an absent term. A reader taking the row at face value learns something false about the term.
publication_impact: If any definition is quoted in the manuscript, an 8.14% chance of quoting a non-definition exists — concentrated in one class, so checking the class eliminates the risk.
recommended_action: Publish the definition_source column unfiltered so consumers can exclude CONTEXTUAL_DESCRIPTION. Document that this class is a passage citation, not a definition. Do not silently delete the rows.
blocking_status: blocks unqualified use of the definition set; not release.

title: 444 definitions are identical to their term
evidence_summary: definition_specificity_flags.definition_equals_term = 444 (6.56%); under_20_chars = 1,168 (17.25%).
scientific_impact: A definition equal to its term conveys nothing; 17.25% of definitions are under 20 characters, at which length a definition is usually a fragment.
publication_impact: Definition-count headlines include these.
recommended_action: Provide documented filter flags; report the filtered count alongside the raw count.

title: The release file and the CDM are partially overlapping, not nested
evidence_summary: 1,150 file rows / 1,073 distinct (term_id,text) keys; 547 present in DB; 526 file definitions absent from the DB; 5,802 DB definitions absent from the file. The terminology_file_vs_db block in D17 reports file 1,150 vs db 5,057 / in_file_not_db 562 / in_db_not_file 4,469 — itself a different comparison basis.
affected_proportion: 526 file rows (45.7% of the file) have no CDM counterpart.
scientific_impact: A reader who treats term_definitions.jsonl as the source of the CDM's definitions will miss 5,623 rows and cannot reproduce the CDM's definition table from the release files.
publication_impact: The provenance chain "terminology 1.0.1 → CDM 3.0.3" does not hold for definitions.
recommended_action: Document the definitions layer as two artefacts: a 1,150-row rule/LLM release file and a 6,773-row CDM table with 5,623 additional LLM rows under run label gap G8. State that the CDM table is not derivable from the release file.
blocking_status: blocks a clean provenance claim for definitions.

title: gap G8 is not a resolvable extraction run
evidence_summary: 6,185 rows (91.32%) carry extraction_run_id='gap G8' with extraction_method='LLM_SPAN_EXTRACTION:qwen3.5-4b'. extraction_run has no row with that id (D10: run registry rows are CATNER_…, 28619916, CATCLEAN_v3, CATLINK_v2, …).
scientific_impact: The bulk of the definition table cannot be traced to a registered run.
publication_impact: Methods cannot cite a run for 91% of definitions.
recommended_action: Document gap G8 as an internal batch label without a registry entry. Do not invent a job id.

title: Verdict labels corrupted in term_definition.verdict_deepseek
evidence_summary: 107/6,773 off-vocabulary values (1.58%), including MENTIO (26), DEFIN (10) — mid-token truncations. Cross-referenced as CQA-D-04.
scientific_impact: Negative-class filtering under-counts.
publication_impact: Minor.
recommended_action: ship the verdict vocabulary; do not rewrite.

title: 987 terms carry multiple definitions with near-zero overlap
evidence_summary: terms_with_multiple_definitions = 987; multi_definition_overlap shows up to 54 definitions for one term with pairwise Jaccard 0.0.
scientific_impact: Multiple disjoint definitions of one term means either the term is genuinely context-dependent or the extractions are heterogeneous fragments. Given CQA-E-02, the latter is more likely.
publication_impact: none, if the definition set is not treated as authoritative.
recommended_action: document that definitions are per-occurrence, not per-term canonical.

title: 18,502 licence-redacted cells ship as full text in the CDM
evidence_summary: Catalogue 3.1.1 CSV carries an evidence_redacted column valued LICENCE on 18,502 rows across 6 tables (cohort 2,580 / sample 2,739 / assay 3,326 / dataset 928 / data_asset 478 / claim 8,451) covering 164 papers / 18,502 flagged records. [corrected by CQA-F-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — this sentence previously read "15,582 catalogue records"; see the amendment note in §7] The CDM has no evidence_redacted column at all. cqa_catalogue_redaction2.json matched each of the 18,502 CSV rows to its CDM row and found evidence_text non-empty on every one, and different from the redacted CSV cell on every one — i.e. the unredacted original. Total restored text: 5,328,140 characters. 3,529 of those rows also still carry CDM gap_evidence (cohort 1,533 / sample 1,720 / dataset 276) — CDM-carried quotes on redacted records.
affected_proportion: 18,502 / 52,400 rows = 35.3% of all catalogue records; 164 / 453 papers = 36.2% of the corpus.
scientific_impact: none — the CDM data are complete, which is what an internal analytical database should be.
publication_impact: major and two-sided. (a) Any statement that the CDM applies the catalogue's licence redaction is false. (b) Any statement that the catalogue release is the redacted artefact but the CDM is not is currently unstated anywhere, so a reader comparing the two will find 18,502 cells that differ with no documented reason. (c) The shipped public bundle (releases/zenodo_frozen/) sidesteps this by withholding the 179 papers wholesale, so the leak is confined to the internal DB — but the internal DB is what an archive deposit of "the CDM" would ship.
recommended_action: Add an explicit evidence_redacted column to the CDM (values LICENCE / NULL) and document that the DB is deliberately unredacted and must be redacted on export; or, if the DB must itself be publishable, mask those 18,502 cells plus the 3,529 gap_evidence rows at load. Either way, state the 18,502 figure in the data dictionary so the CDM↔catalogue difference is explained rather than discovered.
blocking_status: blocks any deposit of the CDM that mirrors the catalogue's redaction policy. Does not block the existing public bundle, which redacts by paper.

title: Cell-level provenance is silently dropped for 3 of 6 tables
evidence_summary: cqa_catalogue_provenance_gap.json. The CSVs carry field_sources / gap_changes / gap_evidence for all six tables, totalling 75,395 provenance entries. cohort (30,583), sample (22,903) and dataset (6,507) load with 0 entries lost. assay (12,159 entries / 4,552 rows), data_asset (37 / 37) and claim (3,206 / 3,051) have no such columns in the CDM at all — 15,402 entries lost across 7,640 records. The CDM also drops evidence_redacted, intervention_category and intervention_agent on all six tables.
scientific_impact: For every assay record — the table carrying DNA extraction, platform, primer, library prep and pipeline fields — there is no record of whether a value was extracted, gap-filled, reverted, or blanked by finalisation. The same is true of all catalogue claims and all data assets. Provenance is exactly the information a reviewer needs to judge gap-filling, and it exists upstream but not downstream.
publication_impact: "Field-level provenance is retained" cannot be said for the CDM. It can be said for the CSV release.
recommended_action: Load the three columns for assay, data_asset and claim in the next build (they parse cleanly — csv_unparsable = 0 in every table). Until then, document which tables lost them and point readers to the CSV release for assay/claim provenance.
blocking_status: blocks a provenance claim scoped to the CDM. Not blocking if scoped to the CSV release.

title: Two evidence flags contradict the anchor on 802 rows
evidence_summary: Cross-tab of evidence_verified × anchor-located over all 52,400 rows: (verified=0, located) 698; (verified=0, NO_EVIDENCE) 190; (verified=0, NOT located) 1,694; (verified=1, located) 49,714; (verified=1, NOT located) 104. Total 52,400 ✓. Per table — cohort 190/0/399/6,485/11; sample 106/0/292/7,118/14; assay 129/2/284/8,117/13; dataset 69/142/147/2,610/8; data_asset 9/0/67/1,913/3; claim 195/46/505/23,471/55 (order: v0-located / v0-noev / v0-not / v1-located / v1-not).
affected_proportion: 802 / 52,400 = 1.53%; the 698 "verified=0 but locatable" rows are 3.48% of the strict-set denominator (20,029).
scientific_impact: Modest in volume, important in kind: the two flags are supposed to describe the same property and they do not. The 698 are records whose quote is findable but which are marked unverified — if a consumer filters evidence_verified=1, they lose 698 good records. The 104 are marked verified but their quote cannot be found — if a consumer trusts the flag, they accept 104 unlocatable records.
publication_impact: Any quality statement keyed on evidence_verified inherits a 1.53% misclassification in both directions. The direction matters: the flag understates locatability by 698 and overstates it by 104.
recommended_action: Document that evidence_verified is the upstream flag and evidence_anchor_status the CDM's own recomputation, that they disagree on 802 rows, and which one to use (the anchor, since it is recomputable). Do not reconcile by overwriting either column in the frozen DB.
blocking_status: blocks an unqualified "all evidence verified" statement.

title: The release's own locatability figure is a flag rate and overstates locatability by ~6.9 points
evidence_summary: QA_REPORT.md in catalogue 3.1.1 reports evidence_located_pct of 88.0 / 96.2 / 91.7 / 94.7 / 95.1 / 96.9. provenance/scripts/qa_catalogue_v3.py:180 computes it as sum(evidence_verified)/n — a flag rate, not a locatability rate. Recomputed same quantity (verified count / row count) gives cohort 91.69, sample 94.71, assay 95.14, dataset 87.97, data_asset 96.18, claim 96.93, which reproduces the published numbers to rounding. But the independently recomputed locatability rates are lower: content-located cohort 94.21, sample 95.94, assay 96.50, dataset 90.02, data_asset 96.49, claim 97.50 — and the strict rates are far lower (35–48%). The formula is also blind to 1,588 rows whose evidence_verified is 0 without a counted anchor (UNANCHORED 1,798 minus the 190 NO_EVIDENCE overlap structure). evidence_verified=1 ∧ NOT_FOUND = 0 and ∧ empty evidence_text = 0, so the flag is self-consistent; it simply measures something other than what its name says.
affected_proportion: all six tables; the published figure is 6.9 points above the same quantity recomputed from the same rows in the cohort table, and the gap widens against any stricter definition.
scientific_impact: A reader taking evidence_located_pct: 96.9 for claims as "96.9% of claim evidence was located in the source" is reading the wrong quantity. The true content-located rate is 97.50% (agreeing by accident) but the strict rate is 35.47%.
publication_impact: The QA table cannot be quoted as a locatability measure. If it is quoted, it must be described as "share of rows bearing the upstream verified flag".
recommended_action: Rename the metric in the next release (evidence_flagged_verified_pct), publish the anchor distribution alongside it, and publish the strict figure with the WHITESPACE class broken out. Do not re-derive the frozen QA_REPORT.
blocking_status: blocks quoting evidence_located_pct as a validation result.

title: Strict literal correspondence is 38.22%; 58% of records rest on whitespace-only matches
evidence_summary: Of 52,400 rows, 30,383 (57.98%) anchor only under WHITESPACE — the quote matches after whitespace normalisation but not byte-exactly. 20,029 (38.22%) fall in the strict set (EXACT/NORMALISED/FUZZY*/RELOCATED). 2,392 (4.56%) are NOT_FOUND. For the catalogue claim half specifically, D18's independent finding_literal_correspondence gives offset-exact 3,510 (14.46%) / normalised 15,195 (62.60%) / mismatch 4,821 (19.86%) / absent 700 (2.88%) / no_evidence 46 (0.19%) — the same shape from a different code path.
affected_proportion: 30,383 rows for the whitespace-only class; 2,392 for outright failure.
scientific_impact: Whitespace normalisation is a weak verb. It absorbs line-wrap, ligature collapse, hyphenation and reflow — and on this corpus it also absorbs the control-byte damage documented in CQA-F-11 (6,027 control characters across 122 papers). A whitespace match therefore does not distinguish "the quote is in the paper" from "the quote is in the paper modulo downstream corruption". The strict rate is the honest one.
publication_impact: "Evidence quotes were verified against source text" is defensible at 96.21% (content-located) only if the verb set is disclosed; at 38.22% strict, the same sentence needs the qualifier.
recommended_action: Report the three tiers with counts and the verb set for each, exactly as in §2.2. Do not report a single locatability number.

title: Sample counts exceed participant counts on 42% of testable papers
evidence_summary: Summing sample.sample_count and cohort.participant_count per paper: 433 papers carry both; 431 are multi-cohort (which is the normal design here — one participant contributes many samples, so a raw sum test is not the right instrument). The defensible test is therefore per-paper sum vs participant total: sum(sample_count) > 1.5 × sum(participant_count) fires on 184 / 433 = 42.5%. The naive max-based test (sample_sum > 1.5 × max(participant_count)) fires on 364/433 and is not defensible on a multi-cohort corpus — the summary figure of 364 must not be used. 2 papers have sample counts with no participant count; 13 the reverse. Separately, sample.sample_count is numeric on 5,246 rows (median 40, max 481,803), and 15 rows carry the downstream annotation IMPLAUSIBLY_LARGE plus hundreds of sample_count=<n>:NOT_IN_SOURCE_TEXT annotations.
affected_proportion: 184 / 433 testable papers; a hard outlier tail (max 481,803 samples in a paper).
scientific_impact: A 1.5× ratio is expected and benign (repeated sampling); the problem is the tail, where values exceed plausible designs by orders of magnitude, and the 15 papers flagged IMPLAUSIBLY_LARGE by the pipeline itself. HMPAPER_000084 reports 670,328 samples against 210 participants, HMPAPER_000417 482,108 / 65, HMPAPER_000222 215,742 / 23 — these are reads or OTUs, not samples.
publication_impact: Any total-sample-count statement (the kind a reader will want, e.g. "N samples across 453 papers") is not supportable from this column without an outlier cut, and any cut would be arbitrary. The paper must not report a corpus-wide sample total.
recommended_action: Publish the ratio distribution and the flag, not a threshold. If a total is needed, report it with the 1.5× filter and its exclusion count, or report per-table medians instead of sums.

title: 190 duplicate dataset groups, 437 redundant rows, on real accession keys
evidence_summary: Over the 1,196 dataset rows with a real (non-sentinel, non-empty, upper-normalised) repository_accession, there are 759 distinct keys, 190 groups with >1 row and 437 redundant rows = 36.54% of real rows. Excluding sentinels (NOT_REPORTED, '', …) is essential: the raw count including 1,412 sentinel-keyed rows gives 194/444/14.92%, which understates the rate by conflating sentinels into one bucket. All other five tables are clean on their natural keys (0 groups). Cross-table data_asset duplication is 69 groups / 80 redundant.
affected_proportion: 437 / 1,196 = 36.54% of real dataset rows; 190 accession keys.
scientific_impact: The same accession is claimed by the same paper more than once, usually with different dataset_title / dataset_role values. This is not a load bug — the CSV and DB agree — it is upstream extraction producing one record per mention rather than one per dataset. A consumer counting datasets per paper over-counts by up to 1.79×.
publication_impact: "2,976 datasets" is a record count, not a dataset count. The distinct-real-accession count is 759.
recommended_action: Report the dataset population as "2,976 records / 759 distinct repository accessions" and expose the duplicate groups. Do not merge in the frozen DB.
blocking_status: blocks quoting a dataset total as a dataset count.

title: verification_status, review_status and link_status carry no information
type_raw: Confirmed defect (placeholder fields shipped as data)
evidence_summary: verification_status is absent from cohort/sample/assay/data_asset; on dataset it holds only UNVERIFIED 2,834 / LINKED_FROM_CORPUS 142; a full-cell scan of the CSVs returned 0 hits in every table, so the column is DB-synthesised. review_status is UNVERIFIED on 100% of all 52,400 rows. dataset.link_status is NO_CANDIDATES on 100% of 2,976 rows. v3_status is KEPT on 100% (dataset +ADDED 142). dataset.last_verified is '' on all 2,976 rows; dataset.data_dictionary_url / study_registration / link_run_id are 0.0% filled.
scientific_impact: Three columns that read as quality state are constants. dataset.link_status = NO_CANDIDATES in particular looks like a completed accession-resolution step that found nothing; in fact no resolution was attempted.
publication_impact: A data dictionary must not present these as informative. Any filter on them is a no-op.
recommended_action: Document them as reserved/constant columns with their fixed values, or drop them from the published data dictionary. link_status for dataset should say "not attempted", not "no candidates".

title: Type columns are uncontrolled free text
evidence_summary: assay.assay_type has 4,156 distinct surfaces over 7,434 non-sentinel rows (top: '' 1,111, 16S rRNA gene sequencing 392, sequencing 132, 16S rRNA sequencing 114). sample.sample_type 1,577 distinct (stool 320 / fecal samples 287 / microbiota 265 / fecal 187). data_asset.asset_type 506. dataset.dataset_type 597 (microbiome 672). By contrast dataset.dataset_role has only 5 values (primary_study_data 1,788 / linked_data 1,025 / '' 152, plus 2 case-variant PRIMARY_STUDY_DATA) and cohort.cohort_role is clean on 6 — so the pipeline can normalise when it does.
affected_proportion: 7,434 assay type cells; 5,809 sample type cells; 597 dataset type cells.
scientific_impact: The module carries assay_type_normalized (73.0% effective) and sample_type_normalized (32.2% effective) alongside the raw columns, so normalised values exist — but only for part of the population and never for dataset_type or asset_type. Any grouping by assay or sample type over the raw column collapses into hundreds of near-synonym buckets.
publication_impact: A table of "assay types across the corpus" cannot be built from the raw column. It can be built from assay_type_normalized at 73% coverage with the residual disclosed.
recommended_action: Document that the normalised columns are the analysis-ready ones, with their coverage; treat the raw columns as verbatim source strings.
blocking_status: blocks unqualified type aggregation over raw columns.

title: 216 values in assay.sequencing_platform are not sequencing platforms
evidence_summary: 1,837 non-sentinel rows / 419 distinct surfaces. 216 rows are not sequencing platforms at all — LC-MS, plate readers, LightCycler instruments, "shotgun sequencing", "GS FLX+". 179 distinct surfaces are not parsed by the platform regex. CONFLICTING appears 162 times. The distribution is dominated by fragmentation of one instrument: Illumina MiSeq 482 / Illumina 116 / MiSeq 94.
scientific_impact: The column mixes technology class (sequencing vs mass spectrometry), vendor, instrument and assay name. A platform-stratified analysis is not possible without manual recoding. Note also sequencing_platform is only 21.5% effective overall (fill 23.8%).
publication_impact: A "sequencing platforms used across the corpus" figure must disclose that 11.8% of populated values are not platforms.
recommended_action: Publish the 419-surface list with a class column (INSTRUMENT / TECHNOLOGY / NOT_A_PLATFORM / CONFLICTING), or restrict to the parsed subset and state the exclusion.

title: Storage temperature signs are destroyed for 147 rows, and the cause is upstream
evidence_summary: sample.storage_condition has 3,647 non-sentinel rows over 284 distinct surfaces. 147 rows / 9 distinct surfaces have a sign-dropped temperature: stored at 80°C (36), 80°C (33), stored at 80°C until shipment on dry ice (29), stored at 20C until … (13), frozen at 20C within 30 min … (13), 80 °C (3), 80 C (3), frozen (<=20°C) (1), plus one long surface (16). Provenance chain, from cqa_storage_signloss.json: evidence_text non-empty on 112/147; a minus token appears somewhere in 58/147 (39.46%); the field-level gap_evidence['storage_condition'] quote exists on 136/147, all 136 verbatim in their own section, but only 2 of those quotes contain any minus at all and 0 have a minus adjacent to a 20/80 token. Of the 136, 107 (78.68%) have a control character or a true minus immediately before the 20/80 token, and the remaining 29 have control bytes elsewhere in the quote; neither-case = 0.
affected_proportion: 147 rows / 3,647 = 4.03% of populated storage values; 9 surfaces.
scientific_impact: 80°C and -80°C are the two most different storage conditions in microbiology (freezer vs ambient/incubator). A row reading "stored at 80°C" is not merely imprecise, it inverts the meaning. Root cause is established and is not the extractor: the minus glyph became a control byte during PDF→text extraction — 6,027 control characters across 122 papers, 220 inside a temperature token across 44 papers, 982 immediately before a digit across 55 papers. The extractor faithfully copied what was in its input.
publication_impact: Any storage-condition analysis must exclude or flag these 147 rows. Quoting "samples were stored at -80°C" as a corpus finding is safe for the 3,500 correct rows; a quantitative distribution by storage temperature is not.
recommended_action: Report the 147 rows as a known upstream corpus artifact with the control-byte explanation and the 44 affected papers; exclude them from temperature analyses. Fixing belongs to corpus segmentation, not the catalogue, and must not be done by rewriting frozen markdown (hash-pinned by corpus 2.2.0).
blocking_status: blocks a storage-temperature distribution. Does not block qualitative statements about cold-chain practice.

title: gap_evidence quotes are perfectly verbatim but unevenly grounded in the value they accompany
evidence_summary: gap_evidence is a dict keyed by field with value {section_id, char_start, char_end, quote} or {"conflict": "A | B"}. Totals: cohort 7,332 entries (6,213 quote / 1,119 conflict-only), sample 8,162 (6,938 / 1,224), dataset 1,554 (1,487 / 67) = 17,048 entries, 14,638 quotes, 2,410 conflict-only; 0 unparsable. Every quote is verbatim in its own section: 100% on all three tables. But the value is not always inside its own quote (whitespace-collapsed substring test): cohort 5,069/6,197 = 81.8%, sample 5,891/6,935 = 84.95%, dataset 839/1,487 = 56.42%. Weakest fields: dataset.data_availability_status 98/673 = 14.56%, cohort.exclusion_criteria 52.69%, cohort.inclusion_criteria 60.93%, cohort.age_summary 77.11%, dataset.access_conditions 59.48%. Strongest: dataset.repository_accession 98.59%, cohort.participant_count 97.59%, sample.sample_count 95.4%, sample.preservation_method 92.74%, dataset.repository_name 92.67%, cohort.country_or_region 96.09%.
affected_proportion: 1,510 of 6,197 cohort checks, 1,044 of 6,935 sample checks, 648 of 1,487 dataset checks fail the value-in-quote test.
scientific_impact: A verbatim quote proves the quote exists, not that it supports the value. For data_availability_status the quote is nearly always in the right section but almost never contains the status word — consistent with the value being inferred ("data are available in SRA under PRJNA…" ⇒ PUBLIC) rather than quoted. That is a legitimate inference pattern, but it must not be described as quote-supported.
publication_impact: "Every field is backed by a verbatim quote from the source" is true at the quote level (100%) and misses the point at the value level (56–85%). The two must be stated separately.
recommended_action: Publish the value-in-quote rate per field alongside the quote-verbatim rate, and mark data_availability_status as an inferred field. This is exactly the literal-correspondence vs evidence-relevance separation the brief requires (§4.1 vs §4.2).
blocking_status: blocks describing all fields as quote-supported.

title: claim carries two disjoint evidence vocabularies and two different locatability rates
evidence_summary: Catalogue half (claim_source='catalogue_v3_1', 24,272 rows) uses evidence_anchor_status: WHITESPACE 15,057 / EXACT 3,510 / NORMALISED 2,139 / FUZZY 1,670 / RELOCATED 1,290 / UNANCHORED 560 / NO_EVIDENCE 46 — locatable 23,526 = 96.93%. Corpus half (corpus_stage52, 21,395 rows) uses evidence_locator_status: verified_normalized 16,602 / unresolved_not_in_source 2,788 / verified_exact 2,005 — locatable 18,607 = 86.97%. Each column is 100% NULL on the other half (D18). Combined: 42,133 / 45,667 = 92.26%.
affected_proportion: 100% of claim rows; the two halves differ by 10 points.
scientific_impact: A single claim locatability figure is a weighted average of two differently-defined measurements. The 10-point gap is real and reflects genuinely weaker grounding in the corpus-stage half.
publication_impact: Any claim-level evidence statistic must name the column and the half.
recommended_action: Publish the two halves separately with their own vocabularies and a documented crosswalk; do not merge the columns.
blocking_status: blocks a single claim-level locatability statement.

title: Dated amendment correcting an unreproducible catalogue record count (15,582 -> 18,502)
evidence_summary: 06_CATALOGUE_QUALITY.md:86 stated '164 papers / 15,582 catalogue records'. 15,582 is reproducible from no table and no table pair (18,502 - 15,582 = 2,920 matches neither). Correct value 18,502 flagged rows over 164 papers.
affected_proportion: 1 sentence in CQA-F-01; scope limited to that sentence
scientific_impact: None; the population was always 18,502 and every other figure in CQA-F-01 already used it.
publication_impact: Prevents an unreproducible count from reaching the manuscript.
recommended_action: Applied 2026-11-05: sentence corrected, superseded wording retained under a 'corrected by' marker, section 7 amendment record added to report 06.

title: Dated amendment clarifying the evidence-judge scope: four figures re-scoped (81.15%/kappa 0.2321/242,158 and 284,325), two crosstab cells retained, one unit corrected (2,023 pairs, not records)
evidence_summary: 06_CATALOGUE_QUALITY.md section 4.3 named the text_value both-valid scope then quoted figures from three different scopes in one sentence. Recomputed from the raw shards by diagnostics/cqa_f_judge.py: judge_summary.json carries judge_agreement_text_values (351,792 pairs, po 0.477, kappa 0.084) and judge_agreement_text_values_both_valid (194,479, 0.85, 0.282), both reproducing exactly. PASS|PASS 159,680 and PASS|INVALID 132,890 are exact cells of the former and are retained. 242,158 / 0.8115 / 0.2321 are reproducible from no scope (nearest all-fields both-valid 241,148 / 0.8135 / 0.2267; exhaustive sweep over 128 field-drop subsets x 2 link modes finds no exact match) - recorded as missing provenance, not fabrication. 284,325 IS exact but on the all-fields scope (mistral inventory, union record set, link-verdict applied; 544,992 cells); on text_value mistral INVALID is 157,011 and llama 2,877. The 2,023 both-failed entries are (record, field) pairs over 1,730 records, not 2,023 records.
affected_proportion: 5 sentences in 06_CATALOGUE_QUALITY.md (section 4.3 x2, 4.4, 4.5, 5); no data defect and no rating changed
scientific_impact: None. The 'judges are not an oracle' conclusion holds under every scope tested (kappa <= 0.282 on both-valid text values, 0.084 across all classes). No accuracy, recall or completeness statement depends on the superseded figures.
publication_impact: Prevents quoting an unreproducible agreement figure (81.15%/0.2321/242,158) or an all-fields INVALID count as if it were a text-value one, and prevents the manuscript layer's own text_value both-valid definition (claims_register.py J04/J05: 0.85/0.282) from appearing to contradict this report.
recommended_action: Applied 2026-11-05: superseded values retained under 'superseded by' markers, correlation section 7 amendment record added to report 06, and a permanent reproducer added as diagnostics/cqa_f_judge.py emitting cqa_f_judge.json with shipped_file_reproduces, the two-scope table, a 24-variant sweep and disputed_figure_provenance.
blocking_status: neither; correction applied. No register row value changed.

title: Cross-paper accession reuse is a contamination risk that was checked and not confirmed
evidence_summary: Of 711 distinct repository accessions, 38 appear in more than one paper (e.g. ERP019369 in three papers). claim_evidence cross-paper = 0; relation_evidence cross-paper = 0; parent-link cross-paper resolution is per-paper and clean.
scientific_impact: Shared consortium studies legitimately appear in multiple papers, so reuse is expected. But it also means an accession cannot be treated as a paper identifier — the dataset key must be (paper_id, repository_accession), not the accession alone.
publication_impact: none, if the 38 are disclosed as a checked risk.
recommended_action: State that cross-paper accession reuse was measured at 38/711, is consistent with shared consortia, and was not adjudicated per accession. Do not describe it as contamination.

title: Two residual single-record artifacts
evidence_summary: (a) HMPAPER_000372 — the HTML redirect stub excluded from the 452-paper analysis universe — nonetheless carries exactly one catalogue record in the CDM: dataset HMDATA_BP_000123, accession PRJNA644520, record_source='LINKED_FROM_CORPUS', accession_valid='YES', evidence_match='NO_QUOTE'. (b) The 142 dataset rows with empty evidence_text are exactly the corpus_bioproject_link records (evidence_anchor_status='NO_EVIDENCE'); they originate in corpus_bioproject_link, not in extraction (D18 confirms 142 of the Q4 accession set are link records).
scientific_impact: Both are correctly labelled; the stub record is honest about having no quote. The only risk is a consumer counting 453 papers with records and not noticing that one of them contributes a single link-derived record.
publication_impact: papers_with_any_record = 453 is technically correct but should not be read as "453 papers yielded extraction output".
recommended_action: Report 452 extraction papers + 1 link-only paper; classify the 142 dataset rows as corpus-linked rather than extracted.

title: The instrumented clean layer is not the layer that shipped
evidence_summary: Clean build CATCLEAN_20261030T173958 (in outputs/results/catalogue_v3_clean) folded 60,424 → 54,986 records, brought papers-with-records 452 → 453, folded 5,580, added 142, elapsed 393.9 s, and materially changed every QA number (datasets 3,234 → 3,064, cohorts 9,591 → 7,451, assays 12,116 → 9,292; evidence_located_pct 71.0 → 87.8 etc.; placeholder cells 3,038 → 8; dataset_accessions_valid_pct 64.8 → 100.0). The CDM carries 52,400 records — neither the 60,424 pre-clean population nor the 54,986 post-clean one. Its dataset split is 2,834 CATNER_… + 142 CATCLEAN_….
scientific_impact: The CDM is a third population, apparently pre-clean with the 142 clean-added links grafted on. Without knowing which cleaning steps were applied, a reader cannot map the CDM's 52,400 onto the clean layer's 54,986.
publication_impact: Any comparison to the clean layer's QA figures (87.8% dataset locatability, 100% accession validity) does not transfer to the CDM. The clean layer's own report JSON also lacks steps/evidence_match objects — that detail lives only in provenance/CLEAN_REPORT.md.
recommended_action: Document the three populations and their relationship, and state which cleaning steps are in the CDM. Do not present clean-layer numbers as CDM numbers.
blocking_status: blocks citing clean-layer QA figures for the CDM. ---

title: No triple carries an ontology identifier
type_raw: Confirmed defect (unpopulated column shipped as data)
evidence_summary: select distinct subject_ontology_id from relation → unresolved (1 value, 25,788 rows); identical for object_ontology_id. subject_entity_resolution_status / object_entity_resolution_status = unresolved_string_match_v1 on 25,788 each. external_linking_status = pending_stage57 on 25,788. In concept, ontology_name is NULL on 185,822 / 204,817 (90.7%); the named remainder is SNOMED 4,909 / MESH 3,551 / NEBRASKA LEXICON 3,069 / LOINC 2,277 / RXNORM 803 / OMOP GENOMIC 687.
scientific_impact: Every triple is a pair of English strings, not a pair of ontology terms. "Bifidobacterium" in one paper and "Bifidobacterium spp." in another are separate nodes; nothing guarantees that two nodes with the same label denote the same entity across papers, and nothing prevents a label from denoting a different entity in different papers. All cross-paper aggregation in this component rests on the single string_normalization_v1_exact method.
publication_impact: The CDM cannot be described as ontology-grounded, semantically normalised, or interoperable at the triple level. Any sentence of the form "entities were mapped to standard ontologies" is false for relation. The defensible sentence is: "canonical terms were mapped to vocabulary candidates in term_concept_map; the triples themselves carry no ontology identifiers."
recommended_action: Either populate the columns (stage 57 was evidently never run) or publish them as reserved/unpopulated with external_linking_status='pending' renamed to NOT_ATTEMPTED. Do not claim ontology grounding in the manuscript.
blocking_status: blocks every ontology-grounding and semantic-interoperability claim about the KG.

title: 68.7% of triples fall into a single OTHER_RELATION escape bucket
evidence_summary: 17,717 / 25,788 = 68.70% carry relation_normalized='OTHER_RELATION' in family escape. Of these, 15,665 are flagged_needs_review and only 2,052 automated_checks_passed. In the cleaned layer the same rows are relabelled into 2,146 distinct typed relations (ASSOCIATED_WITH 1,747, CONTRIBUTES_TO 465, MODULATES 316, DECREASED_IN 276, FOUND_IN 251, INCREASED_IN 249, …) — i.e. specificity is recoverable, not absent from the text.
scientific_impact: Two thirds of the graph asserts only "these two things are related". That is not a knowledge graph in the usual sense; it is a co-occurrence graph with typed edges on the remainder. Any question of the form "does X cause / treat / increase Y" can be answered for at most ~31% of the data, and for the 68.7% the direction, polarity and mechanism are unavailable.
publication_impact: A "25,788-relationship knowledge graph" headline is arithmetically true and semantically misleading. The paper must report the typed subset (8,071 triples) and the generic bucket (17,717) separately; a single total invites the reader to assume the relations carry meaning.
recommended_action: Report the split in the abstract's own number if the abstract quotes a triple total. If the cleaned relabelling is used, publish it as a separate artifact with its error profile (component J) — never merge it into the frozen count.
blocking_status: blocks presenting the graph as a typed relationship resource.

title: The canonical labels cannot be traced back into their own evidence sentence for 76% of rows
evidence_summary: cqa_triple_graph.json: of 34,416 relation_evidence rows, the normalised subject and object labels both appear literally in the stored source_sentence for 899 (2.61%); subject only 4,282 (12.44%); object only 3,024 (8.79%); neither 26,211 (76.16%). By anchor status the miss rate is uniform — EXACT 4,052/5,375 = 75.4% neither, WHITESPACE 18,807/24,702 = 76.1%, NORMALISED 1,644/2,115 = 77.7%, UNANCHORED 1,708/2,224 = 76.8% — so this is not a bad-anchor artefact.
affected_proportion: 26,211 / 34,416 = 76.16% of evidence rows; all 25,788 triples have at least one.
scientific_impact: A reader who clicks "show evidence" for a triple sees a sentence in which neither endpoint is written. The path from sentence → mention → canonical term → triple is not reversible from the shipped columns: term_mention is keyed by span, relation_evidence is keyed by sentence, and the only bridge is triple_mention_ids, which stores mention ids without the span they came from. This is a provenance-chain break, not a truth claim.
publication_impact: "Each relationship is supported by a source sentence" is true in the sense that a sentence is stored; it is false in the sense that the sentence demonstrably states the relationship between the named entities. The manuscript must not claim sentence-level support without a worked example that survives this test.
recommended_action: Ship subject_mention_span / object_mention_span per evidence row (or the mention ids joined to term_mention), so a reader can see which words became which label. Report the 2.61%/23.84%/76.16% split if sentence-level support is claimed.

title: 1,619 triples have no verified evidence at all
evidence_summary: evidence_verified_count = 0 on 1,619 / 25,788 = 6.28%; evidence_unresolved_count > 0 on 1,673; evidence_locator_statuses shows ["unresolved_not_in_source"] on exactly 1,619 (plus 47 mixed). At the row level, 2,224 relation_evidence rows are UNANCHORED and D05 independently finds 2,253 UNABLE_TO_VERIFY (6.55%) — a 29-row difference, which is the fuzzy-match residual.
scientific_impact: For these triples the stored sentence does not appear in the section it is attributed to. Either the section is wrong, the text was lost upstream (the corpus has 6,027 control-byte corruptions across 122 papers), or the sentence was paraphrased by the extractor. This audit cannot distinguish those; what it can say is that 6.3% of the graph has no locatable textual basis.
publication_impact: Any claim of "every relationship traceable to text" fails on 1,619 triples. They should be excluded from or flagged in any evidence-quality statement.
recommended_action: Publish evidence_verified_count=0 as an exclusion flag and report the count. Do not silently drop them (that would change the frozen population).
blocking_status: blocks a 100%-traceable claim; does not block the graph as a whole.

title: The only adequacy measurement available rates 22% of triples "supported"
evidence_summary: outputs/results/kg_2026-11-04/evidence_check/summary.json (16,142 items, 16,132 judged, PREREGISTRATION.sha256 present): R_stated 13,971 = 86.6% (Wilson 0.8607–0.8712) — the sentence states the relation; A_supported 3,549 = 22.0%; A_supported_or_partial 12,932 = 80.16%; A_reversed 236 = 1.46%. D_codes: F 12,722 / H 2,466 / G 944. Relabelled rows: A_supported 653/3,793 = 17.22% vs B_supported 1,911/3,793 = 50.38% (B better on 1,302, A better on 44). Kept triples 5,795/1,776 = 0.3065 supported vs dropped 10,337/1,773 = 0.1715.
affected_proportion: 16,132 judged items (62.6% of the graph); the 22% figure is the strict adequacy rate.
scientific_impact: The gap between 86.6% "the sentence states this relation" and 22.0% "this triple is fully supported" is the single most informative number in this component. It says the text usually does assert a relationship of that shape, but the specific canonicalised pair/relation triple is fully supported about one time in five. Partial support at 80% suggests the failure is mostly in endpoint specificity (the generic label or the wrong granularity), which is consistent with CQA-G-03.
publication_impact: A "22% of relationships fully supported" number is a serious disclosure requirement if any validation section is written. It is a model judgment against a pre-registered rubric, not human annotation, and must be labelled as such.
recommended_action: Report R_stated and A_supported side by side with their definitions, and the reversed count. Never collapse them into one "accuracy".

title: The concept table is 90.7% unnamed and does not support the triple layer
evidence_summary: 204,817 rows; ontology_name NULL on 185,822 (90.7%); source_service ols 62,383 / bioportal 61,280 / umls 54,381 / omop 18,995 / mesh 6,613 / ncbi_taxon 1,165. 11,477 term_concept_map rows point at a concept_id that does not exist — exactly the NO_MATCH_FOUND count, i.e. a by-design placeholder, not a broken reference.
affected_proportion: 185,822 concept rows; 25,788 triples (none of which use them).
scientific_impact: A concept row without an ontology name cannot be dereferenced. 90.7% of them are therefore unverifiable identifiers, and the 7,379 "edges with ontology IDs on both ends" reported by the KG run reflects the 9.3% with a name, not a graph-wide property.
publication_impact: "204,817 ontology concepts" is a row count, not a linked-vocabulary count. Quote the named subset.
recommended_action: Report named vs unnamed concept counts separately; do not describe unnamed concepts as ontology terms.

title: Curated-KG support is real but modest, and is a coverage statement
evidence_summary: gold_kg_check/summary.json — microbe–disease: 622 resolved edges, 82 in a reference = 13.18% vs chance 5.78% (Wilson 0.1075–0.1607); kept 72/466 = 15.45%, dropped 10/156 = 6.41% (kept−dropped +3.2 to +13.6 pts); evidence-supported 10/91 = 10.99% vs evidence-not-supported 40/276 = 14.49% (difference straddles 0: −10.3 to +5.4). chemical–disease: 23/202 = 11.39% vs 9.79% chance, kept 19/145 = 13.1%. gene–disease 0/16. chemical–gene 2/7. Reference mix: Disbiome 59, BugSigDB 60, CTD-any 23, CTD-curated 8. Resolution methods: name_match+name_only 289, name_match+cdm_mapping 205, cdm_mapping+name_only 71, cdm_mapping+cdm_mapping 57 — most KG links rest on name matching.
affected_proportion: 847 resolved edges of 25,788 (3.3%); the support rate applies only to them.
scientific_impact: 13.2% vs 5.8% chance is a 2.3× enrichment and is the strongest external evidence anywhere in this component. It is nonetheless compatible with the graph being right about a small, well-studied core and silent about everything else. The evidence-supported vs evidence-not-supported difference crossing zero means the KG check does not confirm that the stored sentences support the edges.
publication_impact: "Relationships were corroborated against curated knowledge graphs" is supportable only with the 13.2%/5.8% pair, the 622-edge denominator, and the explicit statement that absence is untested. The 90.7%-NULL ontology column (CQA-G-01) means most edges were never eligible for this check at all.
recommended_action: Report as a coverage statement with the denominator. Do not describe unsupported edges as incorrect.

title: 184 self-referential triples
evidence_summary: subject_normalized_label = object_normalized_label on 184 rows = 0.714%: OTHER_RELATION 121, COMPARED_WITH 8, DECREASED_IN 7, PRESENT_IN 6, HAS_RELATIVE_ABUNDANCE 6, ASSOCIATED_WITH 5, MEASURED_BY 5, HAS_TAXONOMIC_RANK 5. The typed ones (DECREASED_IN, PRESENT_IN, HAS_TAXONOMIC_RANK) are semantically impossible as self-loops.
scientific_impact: Small in volume, unambiguous in kind: a thing cannot be present in itself, nor have itself as a taxonomic rank. These arise from canonicalisation collapsing two distinct mentions to the same string (CQA-G-01's root cause), and they will corrupt any traversal or centrality computation.
publication_impact: Minor; disclose and exclude from graph metrics.
recommended_action: Exclude self-loops from published graph metrics and list them as a known artifact. Do not delete in the frozen DB.

title: 247 triples carry unresolved cross-mention conflicts, stored as JSON and never adjudicated
evidence_summary: conflict_flag='conflicting_across_mentions' on 247 rows; unresolved_issues = ["conflicting_polarity_across_mentions"] 160, ["conflicting_assertion_status_across_mentions"] 52, both 35. Multi-valued variants: polarity_variants conflicting on 195, assertion_status_variants conflicting on 87. Example: ["ASSERTED","NEGATED"] 22 rows, ["NEGATIVE","POSITIVE"] 140 rows.
scientific_impact: The triple layer aggregates mentions across papers, so the same triple can be asserted in one paper and negated in another. Storing both values in an array is honest; leaving it there means a consumer who reads polarity_variants as a string ('["POSITIVE"]') will mis-handle the multi-valued rows, and a consumer who ignores it will treat a negated finding as positive.
publication_impact: Any claim-level use of polarity must handle these 247 rows. Aggregate direction statistics (effect_direction_variants is multi-valued on 0 rows, so direction is safe) are unaffected.
recommended_action: Document the multi-valued columns as arrays and publish the 247 conflicted triples as a list.

title: Three status columns are constants, and one of them reads as a completed step
evidence_summary: human_review_status pending 25,788; verification_status pending 25,788; review_status pending 25,788; record_status active 25,788; external_linking_status pending_stage57 25,788. canonicalization_method is a single value on all rows.
scientific_impact: external_linking_status='pending_stage57' names a stage that apparently never ran, yet the column ships. verification_status='pending' on 100% of rows means no triple was ever verified, which is the honest reading — but a consumer filtering verification_status='verified' gets zero rows and may conclude the filter is broken rather than the data unverified.
publication_impact: The data dictionary must document these as constants; they must not appear in a "quality" column list.
recommended_action: Document fixed values or drop from the dictionary. Do not describe review_status as a review outcome.

title: Two model verdicts are stored as if they were validation
evidence_summary: verdict_deepseek: SUPPORTED 20,029 / PARTIAL 4,815 / NOT_SUPPORTED 573 / NULL 220 / UNKNOWN 103 / SUPPRESSED 17 / PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED 11 / NOT_PROVIDED 6 / POSITIVE 5 / NEGATIVE 5 — note the five off-schema POSITIVE/NEGATIVE values, which prove the column was written from unconstrained model output. verdict_gemma_c4: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_WEAK 19,311 / SENSIBLE 5,710 / NONSENSE 683 / UNCERTAIN 84. Cross-tab by family: escape SUPPORTED 13,503 vs typed 6,526; escape PLAUSIBLE_BUT_WEAK 17,711 vs typed SENSIBLE 5,710.
scientific_impact: The two judges are not measuring the same thing — DeepSeek yields a three-level support verdict, Gemma a plausibility label with a 74.9% PLAUSIBLE_BUT_WEAK mode. Neither is human review; both are stored in the release table beside review_status='pending'. Off-schema values (POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, NOT_PROVIDED) show the enumeration was never enforced.
publication_impact: These columns must never be cited as validation. If cited at all, cite as model output with the model name and prompt, and note the 573 NOT_SUPPORTED / 683 NONSENSE as a disagreement floor, not an error rate.
recommended_action: Move to a separate judge table in the next release, with a documented enum and a judge_model column. In this release, document them as model output.
blocking_status: blocks citing any verdict column as ground truth.

title: The removed_relation set is not explicable from its own stored fields
evidence_summary: 6,925 rows, canonical_triple_id unique, duplicate_group_id unique (6,925 distinct groups for 6,925 rows), 0 overlap with relation, canonicalization_method a single value. Composition: 6,222 OTHER_RELATION + 703 typed. Sum of dropped mention_count = 7,286 and paper_count = 7,005 against 25,788 retained triples.
affected_proportion: 6,925 dropped triples (21.2% of the 32,713 pre-removal population).
scientific_impact: The removal rate is large enough (21%) that a reader needs to know why. The stored fields say "each dropped triple is its own duplicate group", which is internally contradictory — a duplicate group of one is not a duplicate. The most likely reading is that these were removed as non-well-formed or as subsumed by a different canonical form, but the DB does not say so.
publication_impact: "6,925 duplicate relationships were removed" is not supported. The defensible sentence is "6,925 candidate triples were removed during canonicalisation; the stored group identifiers are unique per row and do not document the criterion."
recommended_action: Document the removal criterion, or publish the removed set separately with its reason. Do not describe it as deduplication.

title: Two corpus papers contribute no triples
evidence_summary: 451 / 453 papers appear in relation.paper_ids (JSON-parsed, 0 parse failures, paper_count matches list length on 25,788/25,788). Per-paper counts: max 224, median 57, min 2; 15 papers ≥100, 423 ≥20, 1 paper <5.
scientific_impact: Negligible in volume. Worth noting only because triple coverage is otherwise near-total and a reader may assume 453.
publication_impact: Say "451 of 453 papers" if a coverage figure is quoted.
recommended_action: Name the two papers in a data appendix.

title: Zero foreign keys, zero declared types, and no way to enforce either
evidence_summary: PRAGMA foreign_key_list returns nothing on all 44 tables; 866/866 columns have declared type NONE; journal_mode_persisted='delete'.
scientific_impact: Every integrity property is post-hoc. A future load can insert a cohort id that does not exist and nothing will stop it. Combined with the semicolon parent lists, the schema cannot represent a many-to-many relation, so it stores one as a string — and then a consumer must split it correctly or silently under-count.
publication_impact: A methods section describing "a relational schema with referential integrity" would be false. The correct description is "a denormalised SQLite export with post-load validation".
recommended_action: Ship the DDL with FOREIGN KEY declarations and a junction table for sample↔cohort/dataset, even if enforcement stays off, so the intended shape is documented. Declare column affinities. Do not rebuild the frozen DB.
blocking_status: blocks interoperability claims (component M) and any "relational database" framing.

title: A fifth of the schema is semicolon multi-value text
evidence_summary: 183 semicolon-separated multi-value columns; 59 JSON-encoded columns (D19). A looser interop scan (D13) counted 119 JSON-valued columns — the two figures measure different things (column declared as JSON carrier vs column whose sampled values parse as JSON) and neither is wrong; they must not be quoted interchangeably. Parent lists (sample.cohort_id, sample.dataset_id, assay.dataset_id, cohort.dataset_id, data_asset.dataset_id) resolve 100% into existing ids on every part, so the content is sound.
scientific_impact: Resolution at 100% is a property of this load, not of the format. The format has no length limit, no uniqueness guarantee, no ordering guarantee and no null semantics — "" can mean "none", "unknown" or "not reported", and the CDM uses all three.
publication_impact: Any row count that joins through a semicolon column is a count of pairs, not rows, unless it is explicitly deduplicated. The dataset duplicate finding in component F (437 redundant rows) is partly a consequence of this shape.
recommended_action: Document the split rule in the data dictionary next to every such column, and ship a normalised view.

title: 5,237 dangling term_concept_map.term_id values are an undocumented sentinel
evidence_summary: 37 referential checks, 4 with dangling values, 31,198 dangling ids, 25,961 explained by removed_* tombstones, 5,237 unexplained — all in term_concept_map.term_id, all tagged term_status='NOT_IN_TERMINOLOGY', i.e. the same 5,237 rows that component D resolved as the live-term filter on the terminology side (331,394 + 11,473 + 5,237 = 348,104 ≠ 334,231 — see component D's reconciliation).
scientific_impact: A mapping row pointing at a term id that does not exist is indistinguishable from a broken load to anyone who has not read the loader. It is in fact deliberate.
publication_impact: An independent integrity test on this database will report 5,237 unexplained dangling references. That must be answered in the data dictionary, not in a rebuttal.
recommended_action: Document the sentinel, or move those rows to a orphan_mapping table. Do not delete.
blocking_status: blocks a clean "0 dangling references" claim.

title: canonical_term.mention_count is wrong on 40.6% of rows
evidence_summary: 61,839 / 152,333 = 40.59% disagree with the recomputed term_mention count. paper_count disagrees on 11,756 (7.72%), definition_count on 3,316 (2.04%). By contrast all three relation rollups are exactly consistent (mention_count vs triple_mention_ids 0/25,788; paper_count vs paper_ids 0/25,788).
scientific_impact: Ranked term lists, "most mentioned term" statements and any mention-weighted statistic read from the rollup column will be wrong for two rows in five. Because the triple layer's rollups are consistent, a reader who checks one table and not the other will conclude the database is consistent.
