publication_impact: Any mention-frequency figure must be recomputed from term_mention, not read from canonical_term.mention_count. If the manuscript quotes a top-N term list, state which source it used.
recommended_action: Document the column as stale, or recompute it in a derived view. Do not update in place without a release note.

title: 45.6% of term_mention rows are redundant
evidence_summary: 2,505,684 rows collapse to 1,362,888 distinct spans; 1,142,796 rows (45.6%) duplicate an existing span. Component B verified the surviving spans at 99.9978% exact (2,505,628 exact / 0 mismatch / 56 out-of-range), so the redundancy is not a precision problem — it is four extraction sources emitting the same span.
scientific_impact: Every mention-weighted statistic in the CDM is inflated by up to 1.84× if it is computed over rows rather than spans. The terminology pipeline's dedup (terminology_dedup.csv, 166,012 rows) exists precisely to fix this, which confirms the issue is known.
publication_impact: "2.5 M entities extracted" is an observation count, not a mention count. The distinct-span count is 1,362,888.
recommended_action: Publish both counts and name which is used in every denominator.
blocking_status: blocks any mention-count claim that does not state its unit.

title: Three research distinctions cannot be expressed
evidence_summary: research_distinction_probes: has_diet_field false, has_dose_field false, has_effect_size_field false. sample_group_table_exists false; no group/arm column on sample. sample_count_column_meaning = "aggregate vs per-row ambiguity" — the column is used both ways.
scientific_impact: Three of the most common questions about a microbiome study — what diet was the cohort on, what dose of the intervention was given, how large was the effect — are not answerable from the schema. intervention exists as a table but carries no dose column. Effect size is only present as free text inside claim.
publication_impact: The CDM must not be described as supporting intervention or dose–response analysis. It supports association statements.
recommended_action: Document the three gaps explicitly in limitations; they are the honest scope boundary of the model.

title: Q7 returns the opposite storage condition
evidence_summary: Q7 ("stool samples stored at -80 °C") is implemented as storage_condition LIKE '%80%' and returns 603 rows / 191 papers, reproducing exactly. 147 rows across 9 surfaces have the minus destroyed upstream (stored at 80°C, 80°C, 80 C), so the query returns ambient-stored samples as frozen. Root cause: 6,027 control characters across 122 papers, 220 inside a temperature token across 44 papers (component F, CQA-F-11). The sign loss is not introduced by the query and cannot be fixed by the query.
affected_proportion: 147 rows directly; the 603-row answer set includes them.
scientific_impact: A published "N samples stored at -80 °C" figure from this query is contaminated by ambient-stored samples and omits none. The count is right about the string and wrong about the freezer.
publication_impact: Q7 must not be published as a validated query. If the eight-query table is published, Q7 needs a footnote naming the sign-loss artifact and the 44 papers.
recommended_action: Re-express Q7 as a case that requires -80 or excludes 80-without-minus, and report the exclusion. Do not repair the frozen data.
blocking_status: blocks Q7 as a research result.

title: The paper.n_* rollups are mirrors of a different population, not stale counts
evidence_summary: All six paper.n_* rollups disagree with the CDM's own child tables on 453/453 papers (100%), which reads as catastrophic staleness. Component F established the cause: the columns are catalogue clean-layer mirrors. Surplus over the CDM tables is 2,586 rows across 399/453 papers, and n_findings differs from the catalogue half by +405. The clean layer's own per-entity counts (datasets 3,064, cohorts 7,451, assays 9,292) are the numbers the rollups echo.
scientific_impact: A user who trusts paper.n_samples gets a number from a population that is not in the database. The mismatch is systematic (mirror of a larger population), not random.
publication_impact: Do not quote paper.n_*. If paper-level counts are needed, count the actual child rows and say so.
recommended_action: Rename the columns to catalogue_clean_* or drop them from the public schema in the next build.
blocking_status: blocks paper-level count claims; does not affect table-level counts.

title: The published query package is stored inside the release it validates
evidence_summary: RESEARCH_QUERY_VALIDATION.csv is not in paper/publication/final_validation; the only copies are under releases/cdm_v3/3.0.3/remediation/regression/cdm_validation_current_registry/ and outputs/. Eight queries, all reproducing.
scientific_impact: A reader following the publication cannot find the queries where the publication says they are. The release validates itself with a package it ships.
publication_impact: The usability table cannot be cited without pointing at a path inside the frozen release, which weakens the reproducibility claim.
recommended_action: Copy the query file into the publication materials (read-only copy) and cite the release path as the origin.
blocking_status: blocks a reproducible-usability claim; not a data defect.

title: No composite index on the 2.5 M-row mention table
evidence_summary: term_mention indexes are single-column only; there is no (paper_id, section_id, start_offset) index. A span self-join to test overlap is quadratic and killed job 28697992. Five tables have no index at all; 18 have no unique index.
scientific_impact: The most natural question about an NER table — do two mentions overlap — is not answerable inside the database at this size. This audit had to hash spans in Python to run it.
publication_impact: None directly, but it means "the database supports span-level analysis" is a claim about feasibility that does not hold at this scale.
recommended_action: Add the composite index in the next build (cheap, ~minutes) and document that span joins require it.
blocking_status: blocks nothing in the manuscript; blocks practical reuse. ---

title: The public benchmark cannot speak to the corpus, and the risk of it doing so is the largest hazard here
evidence_summary: Tier 1 = BC5CDR (2 types) + BioRED (6 types) over PubMed abstracts. The corpus is 453 full-text papers in 14 CDM types, of which ENTITY (55.29% of terms) and ORGANISM are the largest. [superseded in part: ORGANISM is approximated by BioRED OrganismTaxon, though the transfer fails — 90.8% of that type's gold mentions are host terms and none are bacterial taxa; see correction §1.3.] d20_evidence_tiers.json records Tier 1 with manifest: ABSENT.
affected_proportion: the entire inferential bridge from benchmark to corpus.
scientific_impact: A 90.1 F1 on BC5CDR chemical/disease mention detection says nothing about whether HMCTERM_… "composition of the gut microbiota" is a valid entity, or whether the type assigned to it is right (component C finds 3.06% type provenance and 57.6% flag-vs-type disagreement). The corpus layer's own measured property is offset exactness 99.9978% — an extraction-mechanics result, not an accuracy result.
publication_impact: The single most likely misreading in the whole manuscript is "our NER achieves F1 0.90". It does not: PubTator3 does, on BC5CDR, in-domain. The manuscript must report the benchmark as a model-selection experiment on public data and separately report what was measured on the corpus (offset integrity, type distribution, grounding), never as one number.
recommended_action: Keep the two in separate subsections with separate verbs. Add one sentence stating explicitly that no gold standard exists for the corpus and that no F1 is claimed for it.
blocking_status: blocks any corpus-accuracy claim derived from these numbers.

title: No benchmark covers the types the CDM is built on
evidence_summary: BC5CDR: Chemical, Disease. BioRED: Chemical, Disease, Gene, Variant, CellLine, Species. CDM CDM_TYPES: 14. Corpus volume leaders: ENTITY 89,799, ORGANISM 12,026. [superseded in part: HABITAT, DIET and MICROBIOME are not CDM types — they were invented here. The correct split is 2 direct / 3 approximate / 9 wholly unbenchmarked, and ENTITY is outside the schema entirely. See correction §1.4 and NER_TYPE_COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv.] scispacy_lg produces a generic ENTITY label for every term and therefore cannot be scored on any type at all.
affected_proportion: ≥12 of 14 CDM types; 100% of the microbiome-specific types.
scientific_impact: Model selection for the corpus was driven by performance on chemical/disease mention finding — the two types with the least microbiome specificity. A model that is best at disease names may be worst at taxa; nothing in this suite tests that.
publication_impact: "Models were selected on benchmark performance" must be qualified with which performance and which types, or a reviewer will assume the selection optimized the corpus's own task.
recommended_action: State the type-coverage gap in the methods and limitations. A small hand-annotated taxon sample (200 spans) would be worth more than any additional public benchmark.

title: The top BC5CDR row is an in-domain database lookup, and the pipeline cannot use it for section NER
evidence_summary: pubtator3 † = 90.1 [88.4–91.6], † = trained on this corpus. PubTator3 is a precomputed API result, not a local model; the pipeline excludes PubTator3 from section mode (predict_text raises NotImplementedError) and its offsets are PubMed-abstract geometry, not corpus section offsets. On BioRED the same row drops below HunFlair2 (78.3 vs 80.6, p=0.274).
affected_proportion: the recommendation that follows from the table.
scientific_impact: The best available general extractor for the project's actual task is hunflair2 (77.3) or llm_qwen_fs (69.5), not the 90.1 row. The 90.1 is a ceiling set by a curated resource, and it is not reachable on full-text sections.
publication_impact: A ranked table headed by a non-deployable component invites the wrong conclusion. Either drop the row from the ranking or annotate it as "reference ceiling, not a candidate".
recommended_action: Add a deployable_on_sections column to the table and rank by it.
blocking_status: blocks a "best model" recommendation that cites 90.1.

title: Off-schema entities deleted at write time in the LLM prediction files (invalid_type up to 69.0% of emitted strings); type-agnostic scoring therefore unavailable
evidence_summary: Off-schema entities deleted at write time in the LLM prediction files (invalid_type up to 69.0% of emitted strings); type-agnostic scoring therefore unavailable
scientific_impact: The type-agnostic comparison has no independent measurement for LLMs: up to 69.0% of emitted strings were dropped before write, so a low type-agnostic score cannot be separated from a high discard rate.
publication_impact: Report invalid_type rates with every LLM score, or restrict LLM claims to the in-schema subset.
recommended_action: Re-running the 12 LLM configurations with raw responses retained; or, at minimum, storing the rejected {text,type} pairs alongside the accepted ones on any future run
blocking_status: blocks a pre-specification or losslessness claim; not the metrics

title: No PREREGISTRATION.sha256 for ner_fair_bench / ner_corpus_bench, while the two Tier-2/3 studies have one
evidence_summary: No PREREGISTRATION.sha256 for ner_fair_bench / ner_corpus_bench, while the two Tier-2/3 studies have one
scientific_impact: The Tier-1 suite cannot be described as pre-specified; any claim that the analysis plan was fixed before the results is unsupported for this tier.
publication_impact: Do not claim preregistration for the NER suite. Claim it only for Tier 2/3, which have PREREGISTRATION.sha256.
recommended_action: Nothing, for this run. Declare the tier honestly and preregister the next one

title: The Tier-1 benchmark is the only unchecksummed artefact in the audit

title: The grounding column mixes three unlike measures and one of them is not a vocabulary lookup [corrected 2026-11-05 — the circularity claim in this block was wrong; see §6a]
severity_raw: MODERATE (unchanged — the severity was right, the reason was wrong)
evidence_summary: [superseded 2026-11-05 — this evidence describes a mechanism that does not exist] ~~Grounding = share of extracted surfaces that match a canonical_term. bert_chemical 41.3% (1,702/4,123), scispacy_craft 38.1%, bert_disease 29.2%, scispacy_bc5cdr 25.7%, llm_gemma_zs 25.3%. The canonical terms were themselves produced by a different ensemble over the same corpus.~~
affected_proportion: all 117 (model, type) grounding cells; 25 configurations *(corrected 2026-11-05: scispacy_lg carries no grounding block, so 25 of 26 configurations contribute the 117 cells; the original said 26)*.
scientific_impact: [superseded 2026-11-05] ~~Two extractors agreeing on a string raises the grounding score even if both are wrong...~~ The corrected impacts are below.
publication_impact: [superseded 2026-11-05] ~~"Models were validated by entity grounding" is not supportable. The correct phrasing is "model output was consistent with the project's canonical term inventory at X%".~~
recommended_action: [superseded 2026-11-05] ~~Label the column consistency_with_CDM_terms, not grounded.~~
blocking_status: blocks a grounding-as-validation claim. Corrected finding (2026-11-05). The grounding column is external, so the circularity worry is gone — and with it the project's best defence against the weaker charge that follows. Three unlike measures share one column name, and the manuscript quotes a single number from all of them: 1. ChemicalEntity, DiseaseOrPhenotypicFeature, GeneOrGeneProduct, OrganismTaxon are genuine external-vocabulary lookups over 95 of the 117 cells. These are legitimate Tier-2 precision proxies. 2. SequenceVariant (16 cells) is not a vocabulary lookup at all. ground() returns {"PATTERN"} iff the string matches VARIANT_RE — a surface-format regex for rs…, HGVS-like and substitution-like strings. Its 2.5% pooled rate (1,257 / 50,249 unique strings) measures **how often a model emitted variant-shaped text**, not whether the variant exists. A fabricated rs999999999 scores exactly like a real one. 3. CellLine (19 cells) is definitional 0.0% — ground() returns set() unconditionally. It is a missing vocabulary, not a model result, and appears in the manuscript's figure as a model outcome. Two further denominators the block never stated. (a) Grounding is the share of unique strings, not of mentions: llm_qwen_fs OrganismTaxon is 15.1% of 9,113 distinct strings over **54,139 mentions**, so a model that repeats one grounded surface inflates nothing while a model that emits many near-duplicate wrong surfaces is punished — the metric is a type inventory measure, not a per-occurrence one. (b) corpus_metrics.json ships other_type_pct — the share of a model's strings that ground in a different type than predicted — and neither this report nor the manuscript has ever reported it. It reaches 19.1% (llm_qwen_fs GeneOrGeneProduct) and is above 10% in 9 cells, so for the LLMs a large fraction of "ungrounded" strings are in fact recognisable biomedical names filed under the wrong type. Grounding is therefore type-blind about the error that dominates the LLMs.

Examples of dropped subjects/objects are concatenated strings (100lofathp1cellsuspension106cellsml, 100mgoffecalcontents) — these are genuine extraction artefacts, which corroborates the direction of the judgment.

title: Two in five relabels have no sentence-level evidence
evidence_summary: 6,203 relabels: relabel_evidence='sentence' 3,796 (61.2%), 'triple_only' 2,407 (38.8%). Among generic→typed relabels: sentence 3,895 / triple_only 2,638 / none 41. direction_swapped on 408 rows: 299 sentence, 109 triple_only.
scientific_impact: A relabel derived from the triple alone (A — OTHER_RELATION — B ⇒ A ASSOCIATED_WITH B) is a guess from the pair. ASSOCIATED_WITH is the modal target (2,374), and it is exactly the predicate a pair-only heuristic defaults to. The result is a graph that looks typed but whose typing is, for 39% of edits, unsupported by text.
publication_impact: "Predicates were cleaned using sentence evidence" is true for 61% of edits. The manuscript must not imply sentence grounding for the whole relabel set.
recommended_action: Separate the two relabel strata in any reported metric; publish relabel.jsonl alongside and state that 2,407 lack sentence evidence.

title: 81% of canonical terms are dropped on 1–2 judged mentions each
evidence_summary: 131,682 / 162,409 = 81.08% dropped. Of the 30,727 kept, 5,166 rest on 1 judged mention and 6,048 on 2 — 36.5% of survivors are decided on a single mention. The drop rule is monotone in valid_mention_share (0 dropped terms have share ≥ 0.5), which is internally consistent but circular: the share is computed from the same judge that decides.
affected_proportion: 131,682 terms; and 11,214 of the kept ones whose verdict rests on ≤2 mentions.
scientific_impact: An entity seen once is judged on one mention by one model. Dropping 81% of a terminology layer on that basis is a far more aggressive filter than any published NER curation and will delete many valid low-frequency taxa and methods — precisely the long tail a microbiome CDM exists to capture.
publication_impact: The 30,727-term cleaned vocabulary must be presented as "high-confidence subset", never as "valid terms". The 131,682 are not shown to be invalid.
recommended_action: State the mention-count distribution behind the keep decision; report a stratified sample of dropped single-mention terms as unvalidated. Do not call dropped terms invalid.
blocking_status: blocks describing the cleaned vocabulary as validated.

title: The transformation cannot be re-run from the repository

The judge run is named only by directory (llm_judge_deepseek_v4_flash); its rubric/prompt is not in the layer.

publication_impact: "Reproducible curation" is not claimable. "Checksummed curation with a documented rule" is.

title: Cleaning prunes the graph but does not restructure it
evidence_summary: Nodes −60.6%, edges −62.5%, components −60.1%, but largest-component share moves only 68.5% → 67.8% and mean degree 2.20 → 2.11. 13,682 of 22,579 nodes (60.6%) are orphaned — every edge touching them was dropped.
scientific_impact: A 60% node loss with unchanged topology means the cleaning removed peripheral structure and left the hub-dominated core intact. That is consistent with a well-formedness filter (junk strings live at the periphery) — a good sign — but it also means the cleaned graph is not a re-analysis. It is the same graph, smaller.
publication_impact: Do not present kg_cleaned.graphml as a "curated knowledge graph" implying a qualitatively different object. It is a pruned version of the same one, with relabelled edges.
recommended_action: Report node/edge attrition and the unchanged component share in the same sentence.

title: The layer's type vocabulary is now CDM-conformant, but the conformity is the only thing verified

But "in vocabulary" ≠ "correct type". Whether CKD-related systemic inflammation (DISEASE, unchanged) or any of the 11,614 re-typed terms got the right label is untested.

title: The cleaned layer and the frozen layer can be confused by a reader, and nothing in the filenames prevents it

title: The comparison covers 10.4% of the corpus and that subset is not random
evidence_summary: 47 / 453 papers matched; 667 our-items and 1,537 reference items. BugSigDB curates papers by its own editorial selection, not by sampling. Post-hoc source breakdown: figures 754 items (27.6%), supplements 660 (22.1%), tables 105 (51.4%), text 18 (100%).
affected_proportion: 406 of 453 papers (89.6%) are outside the comparison entirely.
scientific_impact: The 57.27% support rate applies to a curated, well-known subset. Because BugSigDB preferentially curates high-profile studies, the subset is biased toward papers whose taxa are also well known — which inflates both support and coverage relative to the corpus. The direction of the bias is knowable; its magnitude is not.
publication_impact: "Validated against BugSigDB" must carry "on the 47 papers BugSigDB covers". A sentence implying corpus-wide validation is false.
recommended_action: Report the 47/453 denominator beside every BugSigDB number. Do not extrapolate.

title: Nothing was adjudicated; the protocol's adjudication slot is empty in all nine fields
evidence_summary: "adjudication": {} on sequencing_type, region_16s, platform, country, statistical_test, group_size, body_site, condition, group_name. Taxa verdicts are rule-produced. There is one instrument and no reviewer.
scientific_impact: Where the matching rule mis-parses a name (e.g. a genus/species collapse, an abbreviation, a strain), nothing catches it. The report does report both exact and genus-collapsed coverage (23.49% vs 27.72%), which shows the sensitivity is understood — but it is understood analytically, not by review.
publication_impact: This comparison is rule-based agreement against a human-curated reference. It is not itself human-validated. Say exactly that.
recommended_action: Adjudicate a 10% sample (≈150 items) and report the disagreement rate. The adjudication slot exists; filling it is the cheapest credibility gain available in this component.

title: body_site concordance is 24.6% and the mismatch is unexplained
evidence_summary: 57 items, completeness 1.000, concordance 0.2456 (chance 0.050) — 43 of 57 disagree. Compare condition 0.927 on the same 55-paper population. group_name 0.542 (114/249 mismatch), group_size 0.5625 (77/176).
scientific_impact: Body site is a first-order microbiome variable; a 24.6% agreement against a human curator in the papers where both exist is the single worst field result in the component. It is consistent with component F's finding that sample.body_site is quote-supported on only 43.68% of rows and the controlled vocabulary collapses body sites into few values. Whether the defect is in our normalisation or in the comparison's matching rule is not determined — the adjudication slot is empty.
publication_impact: Any body-site-stratified analysis inherits this. "Body site was extracted and normalised" cannot be stated without the 0.246 figure and the 43/57 count.
recommended_action: Manually adjudicate the 57 body-site items — it is a one-afternoon task and it decides whether the defect is ours or the rule's — and report the outcome either way.

title: Group size disagrees on 77 of 176 items
evidence_summary: group_size 176 items, concordance 0.5625 (99 MATCH / 77 MISMATCH), chance 0.0634. For comparison sequencing_type (48 items) and platform (47) agree perfectly.
scientific_impact: This is the same underlying weakness component F measured independently: sample/participant counts are the least reliable numeric fields in the catalogue (184/433 papers exceed 1.5× participant count on the defensible test; outliers up to 481,803). BugSigDB's curator-counted group sizes disagree with ours 44% of the time, which is an external confirmation of that finding, not a new one — and it is the strongest external confirmation the audit has for any catalogue defect.
publication_impact: Never report a group-size or sample-size total. Report the disagreement instead.
recommended_action: Report 77/176 as an external count-agreement measurement alongside component F's internal one. They corroborate.

title: Three "perfect" fields are at their chance baseline
evidence_summary: sequencing_type concordance 1.000 with chance 0.962; platform 1.000 with chance 0.939. The corpus is overwhelmingly 16S on Illumina, so agreement is the base rate. In contrast condition 0.927 with chance 0.050 is genuinely informative, and the report computes and shows both.
scientific_impact: A table row reading "sequencing type: 100% agreement" invites the reader to conclude the extraction is perfect on that field. The correct reading is "the field is near-constant, so agreement is uninformative". The report does publish the chance column, which is the right defence — but the ranking a reader takes away will still be wrong unless chance-corrected values are shown in the same column.
publication_impact: If the field table is published, add a chance-corrected column or drop the two constant fields.
recommended_action: Report concordance − chance (already computed as chance_corrected) in the headline table.

title: Direction agreement rests on 261 of 667 items, and the 60 opposites are not characterised
evidence_summary: 667 items → 165 UNDETERMINED, 261 determinable; SAME 201, OPPOSITE 60 (23.0% of determinable). No breakdown by taxon, body site or condition.
scientific_impact: 77% agreement is a good result, but a quarter of determinable directions are opposite — and in microbiome literature "increased in cases" vs "decreased" is exactly the variable that flips meaning. Whether the 60 are extraction errors, BugSigDB curation differences, or genuine study heterogeneity is not determined.
publication_impact: Report 201/261 and 60/261, not "77% direction agreement" alone.
recommended_action: Characterise the 60 opposite calls; they are the highest-information error set in the whole component.

title: Eight BugSigDB taxa are absent from the taxonomy snapshot
evidence_summary: Overlap 668 distinct taxa; 8 absent from the 2026-11-01 snapshot (1532, 81850, 155615, 424536, 541000, 1505663, 1535326, 1926663); 660 have a name; 0 name differences. Full dump: 71 / 8,479 absent.
scientific_impact: The project's standing claim is "our ontologies are newer". Here the reference is two days newer and 8 ids are missing from our side — so the claim is false in this comparison, by 1.2%. That is a trivial magnitude and a useful demonstration that the question was measured rather than asserted.
publication_impact: Say "our taxonomy snapshot (2026-11-01) lacks 8 of 668 BugSigDB taxa; names agree on all 660 shared". Do not say "our ontologies are newer".
recommended_action: Keep the measurement; it is one of the few places the audit can show a claim being tested rather than repeated.

title: The comparison has no manifest, unlike every other benchmark artefact
evidence_summary: bugsigdb_comparison_2026-11-03/ contains summary.json, items.jsonl, scoring_schema.json, REPORT.md — no MANIFEST.sha256 and no PREREGISTRATION.sha256, while the Tier-2 triple check and Tier-3 KG check both ship preregistration hashes.
scientific_impact: The export is version-stamped to the minute and licence-stated, which is better than most; but the item file that all verdicts derive from is unhashed, so the summary cannot be tied to the items.
publication_impact: Minor. A reviewer can re-derive from items.jsonl today and cannot prove it is the same file tomorrow.
recommended_action: Add a manifest at audit time.

title: Two "BugSigDB support" figures circulate: 50.4% and 13.18%
evidence_summary: Nov-3: 261/518 = 50.4% on (triple, paper) items. Nov-4: 82/622 = 13.18% on resolved microbe–disease edges. Different references (Disbiome absent in Nov-3), different unit, different pre-filter. A reader who sees both without denominators must conclude one is wrong.
affected_proportion: every downstream citation of either number.
scientific_impact: Neither number is wrong; the pair is unusable as published. The 50.4% is conditioned on "the paper is one BugSigDB covers and its taxa were found"; the 13.18% is conditioned on "both ends resolved and the edge type is microbe–disease".
publication_impact: Quote one figure in the main text, with its denominator, and relegate the other to a footnote that names the difference. Do not put both in one table.
recommended_action: Add a reconciliation line to the supplement: 518 items → 622 resolved edges → 847 total, and state why the rates differ.

title: CTD support is at chance, and the two CTD readings contradict each other
evidence_summary: Any support 22.4% (11/49) vs chance 24.2% — below chance. Curated support 8.2% (4/49) vs chance 2.1% — 3.9× on four items. Kept−dropped −0.9 pts (−30.0 to +20.9).
scientific_impact: At the level of "is this chemical–disease association known at all", the triple layer performs no better than random pairing. The curated 8.2% rests on four items and its interval (3.2–19.2) overlaps the any-support reading. Neither reading supports a positive claim.
publication_impact: CTD must be reported as a null result with both readings. Selecting the curated 8.2% and describing it as "3.9× chance" would be technically true and materially misleading given n=4.
recommended_action: Report the null, state the denominator, and note that the four curated hits are too few to distinguish from noise.

title: 46.5% of the KG-check's links are name-only
evidence_summary: Nov-4 microbe–disease resolution: name_match+name_only 289 / 622 = 46.5%; name_match+cdm_mapping 205; cdm_mapping+name_only 71; cdm_mapping+cdm_mapping 57. Nov-3 BugSigDB: name_match 401 / 518 = 77.4%.
scientific_impact: Every one of these comparisons depends on a string equality between our label and a reference name. Compound labels ("gut microbiota", "composition of the gut microbiota") are compared to curated taxon names. A name match can be right for the wrong reason, and name_only means the end was never identifier-resolved at all.
publication_impact: The support rate measures "our label string appears in the reference" as much as it measures "the biological pair is known". Say so.
recommended_action: Report the resolution-method mix beside every support rate. Prefer restricting the headline to cdm_mapping+cdm_mapping (57 edges) if an identifier-based number is wanted — and state that it is 57 edges.

title: Direction agreement rests on twelve items
evidence_summary: 11/12 = 91.7% (64.6–98.5) vs 50% base rate. Same kept pairs, original vs cleaned, n=7: 85.7% both.
scientific_impact: The point estimate is excellent and the interval is 64.6–98.5. A reader will remember 91.7%; the honest statement is "direction agreed on 11 of 12 determinable items". The cleaned-vs-original comparison on 7 pairs (6/7 either way) is a tie and should not be presented as an improvement.
publication_impact: Report counts, not percentages, for n<20.
recommended_action: Merge direction reporting into the BugSigDB paragraph with the raw fraction.

title: The gene–disease check is uninformative and is reported as if it were a result
evidence_summary: 7 items, 0/7, CI −0.0 to 35.4, chance 0.0. Kept 0/4, dropped 0/3.
scientific_impact: A zero-baseline comparison with n=7 cannot distinguish 0% from 35%. Its appearance in a results table alongside the 518-item BugSigDB row gives it undue weight.
publication_impact: Either drop the row or mark it n=7, uninformative.
recommended_action: Drop from the main table; keep in the supplement with the interval.

title: The graph coverage of the whole reference exercise is 3.3%
evidence_summary: 847 resolved edges / 25,788 = 3.28%; Nov-3 items 574. The remaining 96.7% never resolved, because subject_ontology_id/object_ontology_id are unresolved on 100% of triples (CQA-G-01).
scientific_impact: The reference checks cannot reach the graph's bulk. Their positive results describe a resolved periphery, and the 68.7% OTHER_RELATION bucket is untestable against these references by construction — no curated KG stores "OTHER_RELATION".
publication_impact: "Relationships were checked against three curated references" must carry "for the 3.3% whose endpoints resolved".
recommended_action: State the 847/25,788 denominator in the same sentence as any support rate.

title: Kept-better-than-dropped validates the cleaning, not the triples
evidence_summary: BugSigDB +10.0 pts (1.1–18.6); Nov-4 +3.2 to +13.6 pts for microbe–disease; but CTD −0.9 pts (−30.0 to +20.9) and gene–disease 0/4 vs 0/3. Two of four strata show no separation.
scientific_impact: The consistent positive direction on the largest strata is genuine evidence that the DeepSeek selection is picking real signal. It is not evidence that the kept triples are correct — it is evidence that they are more likely to be in a reference, which is what the cleaning may have selected for.
publication_impact: "The cleaned layer was validated against BugSigDB" is a category error: the comparison validates the selection, not the labels.
recommended_action: State the claim as "kept triples were more often reference-supported than dropped ones (+10.0 pts)", nothing stronger.

title: Reference snapshots are dated but not bundled
evidence_summary: BugSigDB export dated 2026-11-03 07:58 UTC with licence; taxonomy snapshot 2026-11-01; CTD and Disbiome dumps referenced but not included in either result directory.
scientific_impact: Today's re-run against a newer CTD could differ. The code hash and preregistration pin the method, not the reference.
publication_impact: Minor; state the snapshot dates.
recommended_action: Record CTD/Disbiome dump dates and sizes in the manifest.

title: The database cannot be ported: 866 untyped columns, 0 foreign keys
evidence_summary: declared_types = {"NONE": 866}; fk_declared = 0; fk_total_all_tables = 0; journal_mode_persisted='delete'; 0 views.
scientific_impact: Any ingestion into PostgreSQL, OMOP, RDF or a dataframe-with-schema requires inferring every type from data and reconstructing every relationship from semicolon strings. That work is non-trivial and will be done differently by each consumer, so two downstream copies will not be comparable.
publication_impact: The bundle can be described as "a SQLite export", not as "a relational schema" or "a portable data model". Reviewers who try to load it into a database will discover the difference.
recommended_action: Ship a DDL file with column affinities, PKs, FKs and a junction table for the five parent lists (component H, CQA-H-01/02). The DB file can stay exactly as frozen.
blocking_status: blocks any interoperability claim and any multi-site reuse plan.

title: Nothing links to an external vocabulary
evidence_summary: 0 / 25,788 triples carry an ontology id; concept.ontology_name NULL on 185,822 / 204,817 (90.7%); external_linking_status='pending_stage57' on 100%; the 5,237 dangling term_concept_map.term_id values are a documented sentinel, not a link.
affected_proportion: the entire graph; 90.7% of the concept table.
scientific_impact: "Interoperable" in the FAIR sense means a term in this bundle can be resolved to the same term elsewhere. For the graph, that is impossible: nodes are English strings compared by string_normalization_v1_exact. For concepts, it is possible for 9.3%.
publication_impact: The manuscript cannot claim semantic interoperability or ontology alignment at the triple level. It can claim a candidate-mapping table (term_concept_map, 331,394 rows) that was never accepted — 0 auto_accepted (component D).
recommended_action: State the limitation plainly; point readers to term_concept_map as candidates and to the unnamed-concept count as the ceiling.

title: CSV and DB are not the same data, and the difference is not documented
evidence_summary: row counts identical 6/6; CSV-only evidence_redacted, intervention_agent, intervention_category; DB-only 13 columns incl. evidence_verified, evidence_anchor_status, section_text_sha256.
scientific_impact: Neither artefact is a superset. A reuser who picks one silently loses either the rights annotation or the evidence anchors. Worse, the two differ on the redaction question: the CSV marks 18,502 cells as licence-redacted and the DB ships their full text with no flag (component N, CQA-N-05).
publication_impact: "Available as CSV and SQLite" implies equivalence. It must say which columns are in which, and which is authoritative per column.
recommended_action: Publish a column-level crosswalk table in the README, and declare the CDM the primary artefact with the CSV as the rights-annotated view.
blocking_status: blocks a "two equivalent distribution formats" claim.

title: A fifth of the schema is untyped multi-value text
evidence_summary: 183 semicolon columns, 119 JSON columns; no escaping convention documented; parent lists resolve 100% but only as strings.
scientific_impact: Interoperability requires atomic values. Every consumer must write a splitter, and the split semantics (empty string vs sentinel vs absent) are not specified, so the same column can yield different cardinalities downstream.
publication_impact: Any row-count a consumer computes by joining through these columns is a pair count, not a row count (component F's 437 redundant dataset rows are partly this).
recommended_action: Document the separator, the escaping rule, and the meaning of "" per column; provide a normalised view or a companion table per multi-value column.

title: The change log ships a revert script that was never run
evidence_summary: cdm_change_log 79 rows, each with revert_sql; REVERT_303.sql is shipped and unexecuted; run_metadata records a promotion from 3.0.3-rc1 on 2026-11-02T08:04:46.
scientific_impact: A consumer cannot tell from the bundle whether the 79 changes are applied or pending. The presence of both a change log and an unexecuted revert script is precisely the ambiguity that a status column would resolve.
publication_impact: Minor, but the methods section must state that 3.0.3 is the promoted build and what was migrated.
recommended_action: Document the state of each change (applied / reverted) and why the revert script is shipped unused.

title: Status sentinels are undocumented, so a consumer cannot filter correctly
evidence_summary: external_linking_status='pending_stage57' on 100% of triples; review_status='UNVERIFIED' on 100% of catalogue rows; link_status='NO_CANDIDATES' on 100% of datasets; verification_status absent from four tables. All appear in the dictionary as columns, none as constants.
scientific_impact: A filter on any of these returns either everything or nothing, which reads as a broken query rather than a constant column (component F, CQA-F-08; component G, CQA-G-09).
publication_impact: The data dictionary must mark these as reserved/constant.
recommended_action: Add a "fixed value" column to the dictionary.

title: No build script ships with the bundle
evidence_summary: 5/5 upstream hashes match and run_metadata pins the build timestamp, but the bundle contains no DDL, no loader and no stage graph; the stage name stage56_triples_canonicalize@2.1.0 appears only as a value inside the data.
scientific_impact: The bundle can be verified but not rebuilt. A reviewer can confirm the files are the files; they cannot re-run the pipeline to see whether the result is stable.
publication_impact: "Reproducible build" is not claimable; "checksummed snapshot with pinned inputs" is.
recommended_action: Ship build_cdm_v3.py + the DDL + a stage manifest in the bundle (read-only). The code already exists in src/scripts/vllm_termpop/.

title: SQLite-only with a non-WAL journal is a concurrency limit, not just a format choice
evidence_summary: journal_mode_persisted='delete', page size 4,096, single file 3.16 GB, 0 views.
scientific_impact: delete journal mode takes an exclusive lock on write; with 2.5 M-row tables, a shared deployment will serialise. This audit ran mode=ro throughout, which is unaffected.
publication_impact: None.
recommended_action: Document mode=ro as the supported access pattern, as this audit did.

title: 179 papers ship withheld pending a rights review that has not happened
evidence_summary: needs_legal_confirmation = yes on 179 / 453 papers: 135 "quotation exceptions and database rights depend on jurisdiction", 29 "is sectioned/re-segmented text a derivative?", 12 "release licence must be NC-compatible", 3 "share-alike may bind derived layers". rights_reviewer, final_decision, publisher, decision_evidence are empty on 453 / 453 rows. PAPER_LICENCES.csv records all 179 as TEXT_WITHHELD_PENDING_RIGHTS_REVIEW.
affected_proportion: 179 / 453 papers = 39.5% of the corpus; 1,367 / 4,006 sections; 9,974,210 characters of withheld text (WITHHOLD_TEXT 9,188,416 + RESTRICTED_NC_LAYER 785,794) = 37.2% of all section text. [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — this sentence previously quoted only the single WITHHOLD_TEXT class (9,188,416), omitting the 785,794 characters on the 15 NC/NC-SA papers; see §6.C]
scientific_impact: none directly — the withheld layer is complete in the internal CDM and every analytical result in this audit was computed over all 453 papers. The impact is that 39.5% of the corpus cannot be shown to a reader, so any published claim resting on those papers is unreproducible from the public artefact.
publication_impact: major. A methods section that says "the corpus is publicly available" is false for 39.5% of it. The correct statement is that the derived annotations ship for all 453 and the source text for 274.
recommended_action: Commission the review. The 179 are not homogeneous — 135 are a licence-determination problem (quotable under exceptions, jurisdiction-dependent), 29 a derivative-work problem, 15 an NC-compatibility problem. They need different expertise and should not be routed as one queue. Until reviewed, describe them as PENDING in the manuscript, not as "restricted".
blocking_status: blocks the public data release from being called complete. Does not block the current bundle, which is internally consistent and correctly labelled.

title: The redaction flag lives only in CSVs; neither database can mark a redacted cell
evidence_summary: evidence_redacted is present in all six releases/data_catalogue_v3/3.1.1/tables/*.csv. A substring search for redact across all 44 source tables and all 46 public-DB tables finds nothing. The public DB adds release_rights (453 rows) and release_redaction (263 rows), which record the decisions and the log but do not mark rows. The 18,502 flagged CDM cells carry the unredacted original.
affected_proportion: 18,502 cells / 164 papers unmarked in the CDM; 0 columns in either DB.
scientific_impact: none — the CDM is meant to hold complete data.
publication_impact: major. This is the same defect as CQA-F-01; from the rights side the consequence is sharper: an archive deposit of "the CDM" re-publishes 18,502 cells that the catalogue deliberately redacted, and no query over the deposited database can detect it. The bundle's protection is a separate artefact (release_redaction), not a property of the data.
recommended_action: Add evidence_redacted (or a whole-row redaction_state) to the six tables and backfill from the catalogue flag; document the 18,502 figure in the column dictionary. Alternatively state in the deposit metadata that the DB is unredacted by design and must be masked on export — but state it, rather than leaving a consumer to discover the divergence.
blocking_status: blocks any deposit that mirrors the catalogue's policy. Does not block the existing public bundle, which redacts by paper and holds at ≥59 characters.

title: The documented 50-character guarantee is really 59, and 403 shipped cells violate the documented one
evidence_summary: build_zenodo_frozen.py:43 sets W, STRIDE = 50, 10, and Rules.leaks() probes every 10th character window. A contiguous run of 50–58 characters that starts off-grid is invisible to the builder and to verify_zenodo_frozen.py, which shares the identical W/STRIDE pair and additionally skips values with len(v) < W + STRIDE = 60. A stride-1 scan finds 403 shipped non-KEEP catalogue cells (122 papers, 42 file-column pairs) containing a true contiguous 50–58-character verbatim run from their own withheld paper — 397 unique to withheld wording, 6 shared with an included paper (permitted). Length buckets 50–54: 291, 55–58: 112. cells_with_run_ge_59 = 0, longest run 58. The same scan finds 759 public-DB non-TEXT cells over 64 table-column pairs (735 non-shared), led by term_mention.normalized_mention 167. The builder's stride-10 probe over that same database returns 0 — proving the blind spot is the stride, not the data.
affected_proportion: 403 catalogue cells / 122 papers; 759 public-DB cells / 735 non-shared. Top catalogue pairs assays.gap_changes 67, cohorts.population_description 38, findings.finding_text 33, datasets.dataset_description 28, findings.author_interpretation 25.
scientific_impact: none.
publication_impact: major, and asymmetric. releases/zenodo_frozen/README.md:67 promises removal of "any other value that reproduces a passage of the paper's wording of 50 characters or more", and line 71 says the independent scan "found no remaining verbatim passage". Both statements are overstated by 9 characters. The measured guarantee is ≥59. A 50–58-character phrase is short; whether it is a legally meaningful excerpt is for counsel, not for this audit. What is documented as verified is not what was verified, and the verification was performed with the same blind spot as the build.
recommended_action: Either (a) change W, STRIDE to 50, 1 and re-run the builder and verifier — the cost is a stride-10 → stride-1 slowdown on 1.06 M cells, which is minutes, not hours — or (b) leave the build alone and correct the README to state the guarantee as "59 characters or more" with the stride disclosed. Do not do neither. If the second, the 403 cells should be listed in the release so the residual is disclosed rather than claimed absent.
blocking_status: blocks any claim that the release has been verified to the stated threshold. Does not block deposit if the README is corrected.

title: TECHNICAL_VALIDATION.md states an invariant that is false
evidence_summary: validation/TECHNICAL_VALIDATION.md:3 — "Redaction removes text only; it changes no identifier, value count or link." Measured source→public losses, all from withheld papers except two, total ≥2,136 identified cells: dataset.repository_accession 1, repository_accession_original 6, data_asset.accession_original 6, dataset.dataset_url 36 (35 withheld + 1 included), data_asset.repository_url 37 (36 + 1), paper.full_text_url 1, dataset.license_or_terms 17, data_asset.license_or_terms 5, dataset.dataset_title 164, relation.subject_display_label 25,788 → 25,218 (570), object_display_label → 24,896 (892), canonical_term.term 927, term_norm 338. Additionally type_harmonization.context 40,141 → 0 in the public DB.
affected_proportion: ≥2,136 identified cells, spanning identifiers, URLs, titles and term labels.
scientific_impact: moderate — 927 canonical terms lose their surface label in the public DB, so a term-level join into the public release is ambiguous for 927 / 162,409 = 0.57% of terms.
publication_impact: major. The statement is in the bundle's own validation document. A reader who relies on it will assume a 1:1 cell mapping between source and public, which is false on at least 63 accession/URL cells and 927 term labels.
recommended_action: Correct the sentence to the measured form: text removal, plus a bounded set of identifier/value losses on withheld papers, with the table. The 927 / 338 canonical_term losses are unattributed to any paper (tables without paper_id), so they need their own explanation, not inclusion in the "withheld papers" bucket.
blocking_status: neither, but it should not ship as-is.

title: Redaction nulls 225 cells on 93 papers that were cleared for inclusion
evidence_summary: 225 cells across 93 TEXT_INCLUDED papers, 41 (table, column) pairs, 174 detail rows. Cause is rule R3: when a 50-character window at the redaction point also occurs in a withheld paper, the value is nulled on the included paper too. Top pairs term_mention.normalized_mention 34, assay.evidence_text 30, relation_evidence.source_sentence 14, claim.evidence_text 12, claim_evidence.evidence_text 12, assay.statistical_methods 8, claim.taxon_or_feature 8, dataset.evidence_text 8. Top papers HMPAPER_000421 14, HMPAPER_000313 11, HMPAPER_000304 9, HMPAPER_000031 7, HMPAPER_000187 7. All 34 included-paper normalized_mention losses are cross-paper (own-paper window hits 0/34), lengths 50–112, median 80. HMPAPER_000406 loses 4 cells this way — including dataset.dataset_url = https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/?term=PRJNA687360 — through a window shared with withheld HMPAPER_000367.
scientific_impact: small but real: 30 nulled assay.evidence_text and 34 nulled normalized_mention cells reduce the evidence base for papers a reader is allowed to read.
publication_impact: minor; the loss is not visible in any shipped report and no aggregate count changes materially.
recommended_action: Narrow R3 to require the window to fall inside the withheld paper's own quote span, rather than anywhere in its text; re-run and diff. Failing that, log R3 subsets per paper so the 132 unlogged cells are attributable. Note the values are not recoverable from the public bundle — they survive only in the internal CDM, so this must be fixed before any future rebuild, not after.

title: RESTRICTED_NC_LAYER is a decision category with no artefact
evidence_summary: rights_summary.json reports RESTRICTED_NC_LAYER 15 (12 cc by-nc + 3 cc by-nc-sa); build_zenodo_frozen.py:131 withholds everything where proposed_release_decision != "INCLUDE_TEXT", so the 15 are indistinguishable from the 164 in the shipped bundle. No KEEP_NC token appears anywhere in the build code; there is no NC layer on disk. Meanwhile the live catalogue retains 1,650 KEEP_NC rows unflagged and 1,645 evidence_text cells in place.
affected_proportion: 15 papers / 3.3% of the corpus; 1,650 catalogue rows.
scientific_impact: none.
publication_impact: minor — but a reader of the summary JSON will look for a layer that does not exist, and the 15 NC papers are described as "restricted" in one document and "withheld" in another.
recommended_action: Either implement the layer (ship NC text under an NC-compatible licence) or drop the category from rights_summary.json and describe the 15 as withheld with reason NC_INCOMPATIBLE. The second is cheaper and honest. Also document why the live catalogue keeps 1,650 KEEP_NC rows while the release withholds the same papers — the two policies are defensible (quotation vs full text) but the difference is currently unexplained.

title: Non-KEEP gap_evidence is re-serialised and silently loses its quote key
type_raw: Confirmed defect (data loss masked as formatting)
evidence_summary: source gap_evidence is uniformly invalid JSON — Python repr, json_invalid on all rows: KEEP 8,687, KEEP_NC 454, REDACT 4,933. Source has_quote: KEEP 7,501 / KEEP_NC 409 / REDACT 4,097. Shipped: KEEP still json_invalid 8,686 (has_quote 7,500); KEEP_NC 454 are now valid JSON with 0 invalid and 0 quote; REDACT 4,933 valid JSON, 0 quote. The quote and conflict keys are stripped by clean_gap_evidence() in build_zenodo_frozen.py.
affected_proportion: 5,387 shipped rows (KEEP_NC 454 + REDACT 4,933) that were pyrepr at source and are JSON at ship; 4,506 rows that had a quote at source and have none shipped.
scientific_impact: none for included papers.
publication_impact: minor, but it is a trap for schema consumers: the same column is pyrepr for 274 papers and JSON for 179, so a single parser cannot read the column across the bundle. KEEP_NC survivors (454: cohorts 153 / samples 135 / assays 154 / datasets 12) are pure {field: {section_id, char_start, char_end}} offset maps with 0 quotes — which is correct behaviour, but indistinguishable from "no quote was found".
recommended_action: Serialise gap_evidence as JSON uniformly in the source build, and add a quote_suppressed: true marker on the non-KEEP rows rather than dropping the key. One line each; the alternative is a permanently unparseable column.

title: 946 extracted values survive in withheld papers, 85 of them verbatim excerpts
evidence_summary: Non-KEEP gap_changes cells whose 'new' value is ≥30 characters: 946 over all six change-log tables (assays 454 / cohorts 226 / samples 232 / datasets 17 / findings 16 / data_assets 1). [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — this sentence previously read "930" with the breakdown "cohorts 226 / samples 232 / assays 454 / datasets 17 / data_assets 1", which enumerated five tables and omitted findings.csv; findings contributes 16 cells. See §6] Maximum in the non-KEEP set is 480 characters (HMPAPER_000079, cohorts.exclusion_criteria; the 1,490 maximum belongs to a KEEP row). Length buckets: 30–39: 513, 40–49: 208, 50–59: 117, 60+: 108. [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — previously 501 / 205 / 116 / 108, the same five-table subset] Of the 225 non-KEEP values ≥50 characters, 85 are verbatim substrings of their own paper's section_text_original, representing 33 distinct strings across 28 papers (e.g. HMPAPER_000123 "PowerSoil DNA isolation kit (MoBio, Carlsbad, California)", 57 chars, 9 cells; HMPAPER_000138 "MoBio Powersoil DNA extraction kits (MoBio, Carlsbad, CA)", 57 chars). [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — previously "224 … 84", the same five-table subset; findings contributes 1 cell ≥50, which is also verbatim] 1 of the 85 also occurs in an included paper; 140 are not verbatim (reformatted, sentence-cased, or abbreviated). Separately, 103 distinct (file, column) pairs / 35,928 cells in withheld papers carry ≥50-character values; excluding papers.csv — whose 9 pairs / 917 cells are all bibliographic metadata in EXEMPT_COLS — gives 94 pairs / 35,011 cells, which is the scope previously reported without the exclusion being stated. [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — the sentence previously quoted "94 distinct (file, column) pairs / 35,011 cells" as if it were the whole population; see §6] The population is dominated by findings.extraction_method 9,255 — a single 54-character constant LLM:Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B:cdm-catalogue-ner-v2-noplaceholder, i.e. provenance, not prose.
affected_proportion: 946 cells ≥30 chars; 85 verbatim own-paper excerpts ≥50 chars, 33 distinct strings. [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — previously "930 cells ≥30 chars; 84 verbatim own-paper excerpts"]
scientific_impact: none.
publication_impact: minor but real. The 85 verbatim excerpts are short phrases embedded in a change-log structure — they are not bulk text, and they reduce to 33 distinct strings. All 85 are under 60 characters, longest 57 (<60: 85, ≥60: 0), which is exactly why the release's stride-10 scan, which skips strings shorter than 60, did not catch them. [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — previously "84 … All 84 are under 60 characters (<60: 84, ≥60: 0)"] Whether they matter is a judgement for counsel.
recommended_action: Add gap_changes to the redaction rule set for non-KEEP papers — the column is a change log, not evidence, and it currently escapes TEXT_COLS entirely. Alternatively null the new field on non-KEEP rows and keep original/source, which preserves the audit trail (what changed, and by which pass) without the value.
blocking_status: neither. Note the 85 are a subset of the CQA-N-03 phenomenon, not a separate class. [corrected by CQA-N-AMEND-2026-11-05-1 — previously "84"]

title: 849 REDACT and 68 KEEP_NC finding_text cells survive, 218 of them ≥50 characters
evidence_summary: finding_text is not in TEXT_COLS — only the W=50 window rule applies to it. Shipped survivors: REDACT 849 (min 5 / median 39 / p95 95 / max 234; 218 ≥50, 178 ≥59); KEEP_NC 68 (min 5 / median 38 / p95 69 / max 122; 9 ≥50, 6 ≥59); KEEP 15,012 (min 3 / median 141 / max 3,007). Source REDACT finding_text was 8,458 non-empty rows (min 5 / median 140 / max 2,598; 7,827 ≥50), so 90.0% were removed.
scientific_impact: none.
publication_impact: minor. The 178 REDACT survivors at ≥59 characters are not verbatim runs (CQA-N-03's stride-1 scan covers them and finds 0 at ≥59), so they are extracted-and-reformatted findings, not quotations. That is a defensible position for a derived annotation, but it is not the position the README takes for finding_text, which is treated as text.
recommended_action: Decide whether finding_text is text or annotation. If annotation, say so in the README and stop applying the 50-char rule to it; if text, add it to TEXT_COLS — which would remove all 917. The current state is a rule applied inconsistently by column.

title: The upload metadata still carries 7 TODO placeholders and the README has author blanks
evidence_summary: releases/ZENODO_UPLOAD_METADATA.json — _instructions, metadata.publication_date (TODO (date of upload)), metadata.creators[0..2].orcid (TODO (add)), metadata.license (TODO: confirm (proposed cc-by-4.0)), metadata.related_identifiers[1].identifier (TODO: DOI of the article (after acceptance)). Shipped releases/zenodo_frozen/README.md differs from src/scripts/release/ZENODO_README.md only at lines 104–106, where the shipped copy has [AUTHORS: add the article citation and this dataset's DOI after deposit.] in place of the full citation/DOI/code block; it also contains [AUTHORS TO CONFIRM BEFORE UPLOAD] (7,249 B vs 7,475 B).
scientific_impact: none.
publication_impact: blocking for deposit only. In particular metadata.license is unresolved: a bundle containing 274 third-party papers under mixed CC variants cannot be deposited under a single blanket licence without deciding what that licence covers.
recommended_action: Resolve all 7 before upload. The licence question is the substantive one — the bundle contains (a) third-party paper metadata, (b) third-party paper text under per-paper CC licences, and (c) this project's own derived annotations. These are three different licensing regimes and the deposit needs to say which applies to which, rather than proposing cc-by-4.0 for the whole.
blocking_status: blocks the deposit. Does not block the audit or the manuscript.

title: The two tables that encode the rights decisions are the only undocumented ones
evidence_summary: cdm/CDM_COLUMN_DICTIONARY.csv has 866 rows over 44 tables and 0 rows for release_rights or release_redaction, which are the two tables the public DB adds. Across the 866 documented columns, definition_status is NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW 644 (74.4%), DEFINED_IN_CODE 143, DOCUMENTED 33, EXTERNAL_SOURCE_DEFINITION 26, SOURCE_DOCUMENTED_MEANING_NEEDS_REVIEW 20.
affected_proportion: 2 / 46 shipped tables undocumented (100% of the rights tables); 74.4% of columns un-defined.
scientific_impact: none.
publication_impact: minor on its own, but it compounds CQA-N-02: the only mechanism by which a consumer can learn that a cell was redacted is a table with no documentation.
recommended_action: Document release_rights and release_redaction first — they are small, load-bearing, and the least ambiguous. The 644 NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW columns are a longer project and should not gate the release.

title: 927 public canonical_term.term and 338 term_norm values are null, and none is attributable to a paper
evidence_summary: canonical_term.term source 162,409 → public 161,482 (927 lost); term_norm → 162,071 (338 lost, a subset). Both are recorded as lost_by_layer: UNATTRIBUTED_no_paper_id — canonical_term has no paper_id, so the redaction log cannot say which withheld paper (or which included paper) caused the loss. Also term_concept_map.mapping_provenance 331,394 → 331,142 (252 lost), same class.
affected_proportion: 927 / 162,409 = 0.57% of canonical terms have no surface label in the public DB; 338 have no normalised form.
scientific_impact: moderate — a term without a surface label cannot be displayed or matched by string; a consumer must fall back to term_id, which the bundle does provide.
publication_impact: minor for the audit, moderate for reuse: term-level joins between the public DB and the terminology release (canonical_terms.jsonl, 165,991 rows = 162,409 live + 3,582 removed_canonical_term) silently drop 927 rows on the term key.
recommended_action: Either restore the 927 labels (they are derived terms, not quotations — the loss looks like an over-broad rule applied to a key column, which is exactly the CQA-N-05 failure mode) or document the null as REDACTED_UNATTRIBUTED. The 43,691 unattributed cells in total deserve one paragraph in the README.

title: Withheld section rows keep their source text hash, which fingerprints the withheld text
evidence_summary: source section n=4,006: sha256(b"") sentinel 453, real hash 3,553. Public included n=2,639: empty 274, real 2,365. Public withheld n=1,367: text NULL on 1,367 / 1,367, text_hash_sha256 retained on 1,367 / 1,367 (empty-state 179, real 1,188). included_hash_mismatches 0, included_text_length_mismatches 0.
affected_proportion: 1,188 withheld sections retain a real content hash.
scientific_impact: none.
publication_impact: negligible — a hash is not the text, and verifying a candidate against it requires already possessing the text.
recommended_action: none required. Record it as a deliberate design choice: retaining the hash is what lets a reuser prove that a reconstructed text matches the withheld original, which is a useful property. The only caveat is that it confirms membership, so a party holding a suspect corpus can confirm inclusion.

title: "No dangling link was found" contradicts a 5,237-row undeclared dangling set
type_raw: Description-vs-behaviour (claim layer) — **the two statements are reconcilable, but only by stating the scope**
evidence_summary: manuscript_draft/02_results.md:29 — "Every identifier, link, offset, hash, manifest and run pointer was checked over all rows. No dangling link, cross-paper link or hash mismatch was found." final_validation/EXHAUSTIVE_INTEGRITY_REPORT.md:16 "0 dangling" (terminology) and :20 "0 dangling, 0 cross-paper" (catalogue). Against that, CQA-H-03 measures **5,237 term_concept_map.term_id values that resolve to no canonical_term row**. Reconciliation. The two are not in conflict once the scope is named: the integrity report checks the declared link graph and the term layer's own referential closure is not part of it, and the 5,237 are the documented sentinel term_status = 'NOT_IN_TERMINOLOGY' (a deliberate marker for mapping candidates whose term was removed in review — see §6.1). They are not breakage. But the manuscript states the property without the scope, and the property as stated is false at the database level.
scientific_impact: None — no query is broken, and NOT_IN_TERMINOLOGY is intentional.
publication_impact: High. This is the specific class of claim that collapses on review: a reviewer who runs SELECT COUNT(*) FROM term_concept_map m LEFT JOIN canonical_term c ON m.term_id=c.term_id WHERE c.term_id IS NULL gets 5,237 and the manuscript says 0. The 5,237 are defensible; the sentence is not.
recommended_action: Rewrite as "no dangling link within the declared link graph; 5,237 mapping rows point at terms deliberately removed in review and are marked NOT_IN_TERMINOLOGY". Add the DB-level check to EXHAUSTIVE_INTEGRITY_REPORT.md as a third scope row. **Do not delete the sentinel.**
blocking_status: publication (accuracy of a stated integrity property).

title: X01–X06 are each used twice for different claims
type_raw: Audit-class finding against the claim layer (documentation)
evidence_summary: 133 register rows carry 127 distinct claim_ids. X01, X02, X03, X04, X05, X06 each appear twice with different values and different sections: | ID | Twice as (Triple ref. suppl.) | described as (CDM) | |---|---|---| | X01 | 518 (triple, paper) items / 45 papers | 44 tables | | X02 | 50.4% taxon in BugSigDB / 16.1% chance | 866 columns | | X03 | 54.3 / 44.3 / 10.0 points | 45 registered runs | | X04 | 11/12 direction agreement | 4 AS_IN_3.0.2_UNVERIFIED runs | | X05 | 49 / 22.4% / 24.2% | 79 change-log entries | | X06 | 7 / 0 gene–disease | 0 unresolvable run ids
scientific_impact: None to any value; every value is separately correct.
publication_impact: High. A [X01]-style bracket in the draft resolves to two different numbers depending on which row a reader reaches first. A supplementary table keyed on claim_id will silently double-key. A reviewer who spot-checks X01 has a 50% chance of finding the wrong value and concluding a number is wrong.
recommended_action: Disambiguate additively — X01tr/X01cdm etc. — leaving the frozen register's values untouched but adding a disambiguated column. Do not renumber (renumbering breaks every existing bracket in the draft).

title: Three files say "80 / 80" while the register holds 133 claims / 127 IDs
evidence_summary: manuscript_draft/01_methods_and_resource.md:7, manuscript_draft/02_results.md:3 and PUBLICATION_INDEX.md:7 all state "80 / 80 match" (or "80 / 80 numeric claims recompute"). The shipped register has 133 rows, 127 distinct IDs, 132 MATCH and 1 STATEMENT. The number 80 predates 53 added claims.
scientific_impact: None.
publication_impact: High for credibility, zero for correctness. The claim apparatus is stronger than it advertises, and advertising a weaker number is still a misstatement. Worse, a reviewer who counts 133 rows and reads "80 / 80" cannot tell whether 53 claims are unverified or whether the header is stale — and there is no way to distinguish the two from inside the manuscript.
recommended_action: Regenerate the three headers from the register at build time rather than hand-writing the count. State "133 registered claims: 132 MATCH, 1 disclosed STATEMENT, 0 MISMATCH, 127 distinct IDs" and cross-reference CQA-P-01.

title: X07 (118 / 2 / 1) has no component-report counterpart, and the 2 failures are undiscussed
evidence_summary: X07 = "validation tests pass / fail / conditional 118 / 2 / 1" and 02_results.md:25 states "118 of 121 schema, value and provenance tests pass; 2 fail and 1 is conditional". No component report (A–N) re-derives the 121-test suite, and none identifies which two tests fail. X08 ("3.0.3 verification overall: True") is likewise read, not recomputed.
affected_proportion: 1 register row, 1 manuscript sentence, 2 unidentified failing tests.
scientific_impact: Unknown, and that is the problem. Two failing schema/value/provenance tests inside the release's own validator are a known-unknown this audit did not close.
publication_impact: Moderate. Reporting "2 fail" without naming them is worse than either naming them or not running the suite: it tells a reviewer something is wrong and refuses to say what.
recommended_action: Enumerate the 2 failing and 1 conditional test by name and their failure messages, then either fix the tests or state each failure's scope. This audit **did not re-derive X07** and says so rather than asserting agreement.
